# Dashboard Components

> A reference library of dashboard components for people building dashboards with AI coding assistants. Each component is one self-contained HTML file (no libraries) plus a spec and a ready-to-paste prompt. All share one validated, colour-blind-safe token set with light and dark themes.

# Square tile US map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** choropleth, tile grid map, geo, click to inspect

Every state is an equal square on a 12×8 grid, coloured on a binned sequential or diverging scale, with a metric switch and a click-to-inspect detail panel.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- You compare a rate or per-capita value across states and small states (RI, DE, DC) must be as visible as Texas
- The audience knows US geography roughly; exact borders don't matter
- You need a compact map that fits in a dashboard card

## Avoid it when
- The value is a raw total that tracks population (show a ranked bar instead, or normalise first)
- Exact location or distance matters (use a real projection)
- You have county or ZIP data

## Anatomy
- Header: title + one-line subtitle naming the metric and period
- Metric switch (segmented control) above the map
- 12×8 grid of square tiles, 2px gap, 4px corner radius, state abbreviation centred
- Label ink chosen per tile by fill luminance (white on dark fills, ink on light)
- Binned legend (5 classes) with range labels below the map
- Detail panel: state name, value, national rank, region average and a share-of-region bar

## Data shape
```
[{ state: "CA", revenue: 48200000, growth: 0.081, orders_per_1k: 31.2 }, …] — one row per state + DC (51 rows)
```

## Interactions
- Hover a tile: tooltip with state, value and rank
- Click or Enter on a tile: selects it (2px ink ring) and fills the detail panel
- Metric switch: re-bins and re-colours; growth switches to a diverging blue↔red scale centred on 0
- Keyboard: every tile is focusable (Tab), Enter selects

## Accessibility
- Each tile has an aria-label with state name and formatted value
- Legend shows ranges as text, never colour alone
- "Table" toggle swaps the map for a sortable list of the same numbers

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0…--seq-6`, `--div-neg / --div-mid / --div-pos`, `--ink`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a square tile-grid US map in a single self-contained HTML file (no libraries). Lay out all 50 states + DC as equal squares on a 12-column × 8-row grid using the standard NPR-style tile positions (AK top-left, ME top-right, HI and TX on the bottom row, FL bottom-right). Tiles are squares with a 2px gap and 4px radius, the state abbreviation centred; choose white or near-black label text per tile from the fill's luminance. Colour with 5 equal-interval bins from a single-hue sequential ramp (light = low); for a signed metric such as growth, switch to a diverging blue↔red ramp with a neutral grey midpoint at 0 and symmetric bins. Put a segmented control above the map to switch metrics, a binned legend with numeric ranges below it, and a detail panel to the right (stacked below on narrow screens) that shows the clicked state's value, national rank and region average. Hover shows a tooltip; tiles are keyboard-focusable and Enter selects. Add a Table toggle that shows the same data as a sorted list. Use CSS variables for every colour and support light and dark themes.


---

# Circle tile US map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** proportional symbol, tile grid map, diverging, two encodings

States as circles on the tile grid: circle area shows size (revenue) and a diverging colour shows change (growth), with a region filter that dims the rest.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- You need two measures per state at once: a magnitude and a signed change
- Big states should look big without hiding small ones
- The question is 'where is growth coming from, and does it matter?'

## Avoid it when
- Precise comparison of the size measure matters (circle area is read loosely; add a ranked bar)
- Only one measure is needed (use the square tile map)

## Anatomy
- Faint square grid cell behind every state keeps the map shape readable when circles are small
- Circle area ∝ value (radius = √value), largest circle fills the cell
- Diverging fill: red = decline, grey ≈ flat, blue = growth; symmetric around 0
- State abbreviation inside circles large enough to fit it, otherwise below
- Two legends: size key (3 nested circles) and colour ramp with signed labels

## Data shape
```
[{ state: "TX", revenue: 52100000, growth: 0.064 }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Hover: tooltip with revenue, growth and share of total
- Region filter (All / West / Midwest / South / Northeast) dims other regions to 25% and totals the selection
- Size toggle: 'Revenue' or 'Equal' (equal circles turn it into a pure colour map)

## Accessibility
- Circles carry aria-labels
- Growth is also written in the tooltip and summary line, so colour is not the only channel
- Dimmed states stay hoverable

## Design tokens used
`--div-neg / --div-mid / --div-pos`, `--surface-2`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a circle tile-grid US map as a single self-contained HTML file with no libraries. Use the standard 12×8 tile positions for the 50 states + DC. In each cell draw a faint rounded square in a surface tint, then a circle whose AREA is proportional to revenue (radius = sqrt(value / max) × half the cell) and whose fill comes from a diverging red ↔ grey ↔ blue scale for year-over-year growth, symmetric around zero. Put the state abbreviation inside the circle when it fits, choosing white or dark text by fill luminance, otherwise just below it in muted text. Add a size legend (three nested circles with values) and a diverging colour legend with signed % labels. Add a region segmented control that dims other regions to 25% opacity and updates a summary line ('South: $X revenue, +Y% growth'). Add a Size toggle for Revenue vs Equal circles. Hover tooltips show revenue, growth and share of total. Use CSS variables for every colour and support light and dark themes.


---

# Hex tile US map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** hexbin, tile grid map, categorical, legend filter

A hexagon tile map coloured by a category (the leading sales channel per state), where the legend doubles as a filter and shows each category's count.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Each state has one winning category (top channel, party, plan tier, vendor)
- You want a softer, more organic map than squares with the same equal-area fairness
- Three or fewer categories — the colour set stays distinguishable for colour-blind readers

## Avoid it when
- More than 3–4 categories (fold extras into 'Other' or use small multiples)
- The value is continuous (use a sequential tile map)

## Anatomy
- Pointy-top hexagons; odd rows shifted half a hex so neighbours nest
- Categorical fills in fixed order (slot 1, 2, 3); never re-coloured when filtered
- 2px surface-coloured gap between hexes
- Legend chips: swatch + label + count, clickable
- Margin of victory shown as fill opacity is NOT used — opacity is reserved for filtering

## Data shape
```
[{ state: "OH", channel: "Retail", share: 0.46 }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Click a legend chip to isolate that category (others drop to 15%); click again to reset
- Hover a hex: state, winning channel and its share
- Keyboard: legend chips are buttons

## Accessibility
- Legend chips are real buttons with aria-pressed
- Category name always appears in the tooltip and legend text
- Uses only the first three categorical slots, which pass all-pairs colour-blind checks

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a hexagon tile-grid US map in one self-contained HTML file (no libraries). Use pointy-top hexagons laid out from the standard 12×8 US tile grid, shifting odd rows right by half a hex width so tiles nest; leave a 2px gap. Colour each state by its leading category (e.g. top sales channel: Online, Retail, Partner) using the first three categorical colour tokens in fixed order. Centre the state abbreviation with text colour chosen by fill luminance. Below the title, render legend chips (swatch, label, count of states) that act as filters: clicking one dims every other category to 15% opacity, clicking again resets; colours never change when filtering. Hover tooltips show the state, the winning category and its share. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.


---

# Sparkline tile US map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** small multiples, tile grid map, trend, sparkline

Each state tile holds its own 24-month trend line, so the map shows shape over time instead of a single number; a filter highlights rising or falling states.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The story is how each state's trend moved, not where the level is highest
- You want regional patterns in trajectories (e.g. the South rising, the Midwest flat)
- There is room for ~60px tiles

## Avoid it when
- Phone-width layouts (tiles become too small for lines; switch to a ranked list of sparklines)
- Exact values matter (use a table with sparklines)

## Anatomy
- Tile background in surface tint; state code top-left; % change bottom-right
- Each line indexed to its own first month (local y-scale) — shape, not size, is compared
- Line in the accent colour, end dot ≥ 8px with a surface ring
- Tiles with the selected trend stay full strength, the rest fade

## Data shape
```
[{ state: "GA", series: [100, 101.4, …24 monthly values] }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Highlight control: All / Rising / Falling / Flat
- Hover a tile: tooltip with first and last value and % change, plus a crosshair-free enlarged line

## Accessibility
- % change printed on each tile so trend direction is never colour-only
- aria-label per tile with start, end and change

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--surface-2`, `--up`, `--down`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a sparkline tile-grid US map in a single self-contained HTML file. Use the standard 12×8 US tile grid; each state tile is a rounded square in a light surface tint containing: the state code top-left (small, semibold), a 24-month sparkline filling the middle (2px accent line, a light 10% area wash, an end dot with a surface-coloured ring), and the % change bottom-right in green or red text with a ▲/▼ glyph. Each sparkline uses its own y-scale so shapes are comparable. Add a segmented control (All / Rising / Falling / Flat, where flat = within ±2%) that fades non-matching tiles to 20% opacity, and a summary count. Hover shows start, end and change. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.


---

# Ring meters with severity

**Category:** Gauges · **Tags:** donut gauge, utilisation, capacity, meter

A grid of 270° ring meters for capacity-style metrics, where the fill colour carries severity (accent → warning → critical) and each ring shows used / total underneath.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing utilisation of a fixed capacity: quota, storage, budget spent, seats
- Several resources share the same 0–100% scale
- Severity bands are well understood (e.g. >80% warning, >95% critical)

## Avoid it when
- Values can exceed 100% meaningfully (use activity rings or a bullet chart)
- Comparing values that aren't percentages of a whole

## Anatomy
- 270° ring (open at the bottom) so the end is easy to judge, 10px stroke, round caps
- Track is a lighter step of the fill's own hue so state reads across the whole ring
- Fill: accent below 75%, warning 75–90%, critical above 90%
- Centre: % used (semibold) and the resource name
- Below: used / total in absolute units and an icon + word status

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Storage", used: 7.4, total: 10, unit: "TB" }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Workspace switch re-draws all rings
- Hover a ring: used, total, headroom left

## Accessibility
- role=meter with aria-valuenow
- Severity has an icon and word next to it
- Percent is printed, never only implied by the arc

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--warn`, `--crit`, `--track`, `--surface-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a responsive grid of 270° ring meters (open at the bottom) as one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. Each ring has a 10px round-capped stroke; the track is a pale tint of the same hue as the fill; the fill colour encodes severity — accent under 75%, warning 75–90%, critical over 90% — and the track tints follow. Centre the percentage (semibold, ~22px) with the resource name under it; below the ring print 'used / total unit' and a status with an icon (● Healthy, ▲ High, ■ Critical). Add a segmented control to switch between workspaces with different values. Hover shows used, total and headroom. role=meter with aria values. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.


---

# Activity rings (goal tracker)

**Category:** Gauges · **Tags:** concentric rings, goals, daily targets, overflow

Three concentric rings track daily goals (calls, demos, deals); rings can lap past 100%, and a week strip of mini rings lets you pick the day.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- A person or team has 2–3 daily or weekly goals with different units
- Over-achievement should be visible (a second lap)
- A motivational, personal view — sales reps, coaches, habit trackers

## Avoid it when
- Comparing goals across many people (use a table or bullet charts)
- More than 3 rings — inner rings get too short to read

## Anatomy
- Three concentric 270°→full rings, outer to inner = series slots 1, 2, 3 in fixed order
- Track = 18% tint of each ring's colour
- Progress past 100% keeps going as a second lap with a surface-coloured ring on its end cap
- Legend column: swatch, goal name, value / goal and % — the legend is the readout
- Week strip: seven small ring sets; the selected day is outlined

## Data shape
```
{ goals: [{ name: "Calls", goal: 40 }, …], days: [{ date: "Mon", values: [38, 3, 1] }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Click a day in the strip (or use arrow keys) to show it in the big rings
- Hover a ring: value, goal and %

## Accessibility
- Values and % written in the legend — rings are never the only channel
- Day buttons are real buttons with aria-pressed and arrow-key navigation
- Uses the three categorical slots validated for all-pairs colour-blind separation

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an activity-rings goal tracker in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. Draw three concentric rings (outer → inner = categorical colours 1, 2, 3) on tracks that are 18% tints of each colour, 14px wide with round caps, starting at 12 o'clock and running clockwise; if progress exceeds 100%, continue drawing a second lap on top with a 2px surface-coloured outline around its end cap so the overlap is visible. To the right, a legend that doubles as the readout: swatch, goal name, 'value / goal' and percentage. Under it, a strip of seven small ring sets (Mon–Sun) as buttons; clicking one (or arrow keys) loads that day into the big rings, and the selected day is outlined. Hover tooltips on rings. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.


---

# Bullet chart list

**Category:** Gauges · **Tags:** bullet graph, target vs actual, qualitative bands, Stephen Few

A stack of horizontal bullet charts — actual bar, target tick, prior-year marker and three grey performance bands — with % of target and a sort control.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Many metrics need actual vs target in little space (the dense replacement for a wall of gauges)
- Each metric has its own scale and its own 'poor / satisfactory / good' bands
- You want prior period as a secondary comparison

## Avoid it when
- There is no target or band to compare against (use a plain bar)
- The audience needs a trend (pair with a sparkline column)

## Anatomy
- Label column: metric name + unit
- Three bands in stepped neutral greys (darkest = poor) behind the bar, full row height
- Actual bar: one-third of band height, accent colour, 4px rounded end
- Target: 2px ink tick, taller than the bar
- Prior year: small hollow diamond marker
- Value + % of target on the right; % in up/down text colour

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Revenue", unit: "$K", actual: 270, target: 250, prior: 231, zones: [150, 225, 300] }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Sort: original order, % of target, or gap to target
- Hover a row: actual, target, prior year and band reached

## Accessibility
- % of target written as text with a ▲/▼ glyph
- Each row has an aria-label summarising actual vs target

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--surface-2`, `--axis`, `--ink`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a list of horizontal bullet charts in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG (no libraries). One row per metric, each with its own scale from 0 to the top of its range. In each row draw: three qualitative bands as stepped neutral greys (darkest = poor) spanning the row height; the actual value as an accent bar one-third the band height with a 4px rounded end; a 2px ink target tick taller than the bar; a small hollow diamond for the prior-year value. A left label column shows the metric name and unit; a right column shows the actual value and % of target with ▲/▼ in success/danger text colours. Add a segmented sort control (Default / % of target / Gap) and hover tooltips. Rows animate to their new positions when sorted. Include a tiny legend explaining bar, tick, diamond and bands. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.


---

# KPI cards with sparkline

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** stat tile, sparkline, delta badge, period comparison

The workhorse KPI row: label, big value, signed delta vs the previous period, and a sparkline of the current period over a grey ghost of the previous one, with a 7D / 30D / 90D switch.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The top row of almost any dashboard: 3–5 headline numbers
- Readers need both 'how much' and 'which way' at a glance
- Comparing to the immediately previous period is meaningful

## Avoid it when
- More than ~6 KPIs (group them or use a table with sparklines)
- There is a single headline number (use a hero KPI)

## Anatomy
- Label in secondary ink, sentence case, no colon
- Value: 28px semibold, auto-compacted ($1.28M, 12.9K), proportional figures
- Delta: signed %, ▲/▼, colour = direction × whether up is good, followed by 'vs prev. 30 days' in muted text
- Sparkline: current period as a 2px accent line with a 10% area wash; previous period as a 1.5px grey line behind it
- Crosshair readout on hover

## Data shape
```
{ label: "Revenue", fmt: "$", upIsGood: true, daily: [ …180 numbers, oldest first ] } — current and previous periods are sliced from the same series
```

## Interactions
- Period switch re-slices every card (7 / 30 / 90 days)
- Hover a sparkline: crosshair dot and tooltip with the day's value and the same day last period

## Accessibility
- Delta direction carried by ▲/▼ and sign, not just colour
- Each card is an article with an aria-label summarising value and change
- Sparkline is decorative-plus: the numbers it encodes are in the tooltip and label

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--de-emph`, `--up`, `--down`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a responsive row of four KPI cards in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. Each card: a label in secondary ink, the value in 28px semibold (auto-compact: $1.28M, 12.9K), a delta line with ▲/▼, signed percent and 'vs prev. N days' (green when the change is good, red when bad — respect metrics where down is good, like refund rate), and a 48px-tall sparkline of the current period as a 2px accent line with a 10% area wash, drawn over the previous period as a thinner grey line. Generate 180 days of seeded synthetic data per metric and add a 7D / 30D / 90D segmented control that re-slices current vs previous period and recomputes totals and deltas (sum for counts, mean for rates). Hovering a sparkline shows a dot and a tooltip with that day's value and the same day in the previous period. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.


---

# KPI cards with target and pace

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** progress, month to date, pacing, forecast

Month-to-date KPI cards that show actual vs target as a progress meter, plus a pace marker for where you should be today and a projected month-end finish.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Goals reset each month or quarter and the question is 'are we on pace?'
- Sales quotas, fundraising, hiring plans, content output
- You want an early warning before the period ends

## Avoid it when
- Values are not cumulative within the period (rates, averages)
- There is no target

## Anatomy
- Value as a fraction: actual (semibold) / target (muted)
- Progress meter: 8px track in a pale accent, fill in accent; fill switches to warning when behind pace by >5%
- Pace marker: 2px ink tick at (day ÷ days in month) × target, labelled 'Today'
- Status line with icon: ✓ Ahead of pace / ! Behind pace, by how much
- Projected finish: actual ÷ day × days in month, shown vs target

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "New ARR", target: 400000, daily: [ …30 numbers ] }, …]
```

## Interactions
- 'Day of month' slider replays the month so you can see pacing change
- Hover a meter: actual, expected by today, projected finish

## Accessibility
- role=progressbar on each meter with aria-valuenow / max
- Status is an icon + sentence, not just the meter colour
- Slider has a visible label and value

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--warn`, `--track`, `--ink`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build month-to-date KPI cards with pacing in one self-contained HTML file. Each card shows the metric name, then actual / target as a fraction (actual semibold, target muted), an 8px progress meter (pale accent track, accent fill that turns to the warning colour when more than 5% behind pace), a 2px ink pace tick at (day ÷ days in month) × target labelled 'Today', a status line with an icon (✓ Ahead of pace by X / ! Behind pace by X) and a projected month-end finish (actual ÷ day × days) vs target. Generate seeded daily data for 30 days and add a labelled 'Day of month' range slider that recomputes everything as if it were that day. Meters are role=progressbar. Hover tooltips with actual, expected and projected. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.


---

# KPI cards with year-over-year columns

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** month selector, prior year, mini column chart, click to drill

KPI cards whose mini column chart doubles as a month picker: grey columns for the year, the selected month in accent, prior-year ticks above each, and the headline value follows your click.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Monthly business reviews: 'how did March do, and vs last March?'
- Seasonality matters, so year-over-year beats month-over-month
- You want the KPI and its 12-month context in one card

## Avoid it when
- Daily or weekly granularity (use a sparkline card)
- There is no prior-year data

## Anatomy
- Header: label + selected month name
- Value (semibold 26px) and YoY delta with ▲/▼
- 12 mini columns (max 16px wide, 4px rounded top, 2px gaps): de-emphasis grey, selected month in accent
- Prior-year value per month as a short 2px ink tick
- Month initials under the columns

## Data shape
```
[{ label: "Bookings", cy: [12 monthly values], py: [12 monthly values], upIsGood: true }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Click any column (in any card) to select that month across all cards
- Arrow keys move the selection when a card has focus
- Hover a column: this year, last year and the change

## Accessibility
- Columns are focusable via the card; arrow keys change month
- Delta text includes direction glyph
- aria-live region announces the selected month

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--de-emph`, `--ink`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build three KPI cards with year-over-year mini columns in one self-contained HTML file. Each card: label and the selected month name in muted text, the selected month's value (26px semibold), a YoY delta with ▲/▼ (green if good, red if bad, respecting metrics where down is good), and a 12-month column chart (bars ≤16px wide, 4px rounded tops, square at the baseline, de-emphasis grey) where the selected month is the accent colour and each month has a short 2px ink tick at last year's value. Month initials sit under the columns. Clicking a column selects that month in every card; when a card is focused, Left/Right arrow keys move the month. Hover tooltips show this year, last year and the change. Seeded synthetic data with seasonality. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.


---

# KPI cards with breakdown bar

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** part to whole, stacked bar, composition, legend highlight

A KPI total with a single 100% stacked bar beneath it showing what it's made of; hovering a segment or legend row highlights the pair and shows its share.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The total matters and so does its mix (revenue by channel, tickets by tier, spend by team)
- There are 2–5 parts
- You need composition without a donut taking up a whole panel

## Avoid it when
- More than 5 parts (fold the tail into 'Other')
- The parts don't add up to the total (overlapping categories)

## Anatomy
- Label, value (28px semibold) and delta
- One 12px-tall 100% bar; segments in categorical order with 2px surface gaps; outer ends rounded 4px
- Legend list under the bar: swatch, name, value, share — right-aligned tabular numbers
- Highlight: hovered part stays full strength, others drop to 30%

## Data shape
```
{ label: "Revenue", total: 1280000, parts: [{ name: "Online", value: 610000 }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a segment or a legend row: both highlight together and a tooltip shows value and share
- Toggle Value / Share in the legend

## Accessibility
- Every value is in the legend as text — the bar is a summary, not the only carrier
- Legend rows are focusable and highlight on focus as well as hover

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--surface`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt

# Hero KPI with expected range

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** hero number, anomaly, expected range, narrative, Pulse style

One big number with its change, a trend line drawn inside an expected-range band, and a generated sentence that says whether the latest value is normal, unusually high or unusually low.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- One metric deserves the spotlight (the north-star or the metric a page is about)
- Readers need to know if a move is noise or signal
- You want the dashboard to explain itself in words

## Avoid it when
- Several metrics are equally important (use a KPI row)
- Too little history to estimate a range (< ~8 periods)

## Anatomy
- Hero value ≥ 48px semibold, exactly one per view
- Delta vs prior week with ▲/▼ and vs-period text
- Narrative sentence built from the data; the key phrase in ink weight
- Line: 2px accent; expected range: band of mean ± 2σ of the trailing 8 weeks in a 12% accent wash
- Latest point: 8px marker with a surface ring; points outside the band get a hollow ring

## Data shape
```
{ metric: "Weekly active users", weekly: [ …26 numbers ] }
```

## Interactions
- Metric switch rebuilds the number, sentence and band
- Hover the line: crosshair with value, expected range and whether it was inside

## Accessibility
- The sentence states the conclusion in words
- Outliers are marked by shape (hollow ring), not colour alone

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

Below, a 26-week line chart (2px accent line) inside an expected-range band computed per week as mean ± 2 standard deviations of the previous 8 weeks, drawn as a 12% accent wash; mark the latest point with an 8px dot and a surface ring and give any out-of-band week a hollow ring. # Status KPI cards

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** threshold, ops board, status colour, alerting, sparkline

The standard KPI card (label, big value, delta, sparkline) colour-coded by status — OK, Warning or Critical against configurable thresholds — with a switch between a full-colour tint and a left-edge highlight only.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- An ops or on-call view where 'what needs attention?' matters as much as the numbers
- Every metric has agreed warning and critical thresholds
- You want status cards that sit next to ordinary KPI cards without looking like a different system

## Avoid it when
- Business reporting where most metrics have no threshold (status colour becomes decoration)
- Comparing magnitudes across cards (status hides scale)

## Anatomy
- Same card as the KPI row: 1px hairline border, 10px radius, label in secondary ink, 28px semibold value with unit, delta line, 48px sparkline
- Status badge top-right: icon + word (✓ OK, ! Warning, ✕ Critical) — status is never colour alone
- Full colour mode: background is a 12% tint of the status colour and the border a 40% tint
- Left edge mode: neutral card with a 4px status-coloured edge on the left
- Sparkline: 2px line and 10% area wash in the status colour, warning and critical thresholds as faint dashed lines, end dot with a surface ring
- Delta: change vs 30 minutes ago with ▲/▼, green when it moved the good way, red when the bad way
- Footer: the threshold rule as text ('warn ≥ 250 ms · crit ≥ 400 ms')

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "p95 latency", unit: "ms", warn: 250, crit: 400, higherIsWorse: true, last30: [ … ] }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Style switch: Full colour / Left edge
- Threshold profile switch (Default / Strict) re-evaluates every card
- 'Simulate tick' appends a new point to every series
- Hover a sparkline: value at that minute; hover the card header: thresholds and distance to the next state

## Accessibility
- Status as icon + word in the badge
- Each card's aria-label states value and status; a polite live region announces status changes
- Status colours are reserved and never used for series; value text stays in ink

## Design tokens used
`--good / --warn / --crit`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--grid`, `--surface`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a row of status-coded KPI cards in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. Each card uses the standard KPI card layout — 1px hairline border, 10px radius, a secondary-ink label, a 28px semibold value with its unit, a delta line (▲/▼ change vs 30 minutes ago, green when it moved the good way and red when the bad way, respecting higher-is-worse vs lower-is-worse metrics) and a 48px sparkline — plus a status badge top-right with an icon and word (✓ OK, ! Warning, ✕ Critical) from warning and critical thresholds. Colour the card by status in one of two modes chosen with a segmented control: Full colour (background = 12% tint of the status colour, border = 40% tint) or Left edge (neutral card with a 4px status-coloured left edge). Draw the sparkline as a 2px line with a 10% area wash in the status colour, the two thresholds as faint dashed lines and an end dot with a surface ring. Add a footer stating the threshold rule, a threshold-profile control (Default / Strict), a 'Simulate tick' button that appends a random-walk point to every card, and an aria-live region announcing status changes. Keep all text in ink tokens, never in the status colour. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

A full-featured accounts table: search, region and status filters, sortable columns, pagination, inline MRR bars, status pills, expandable rows with a 12-month trend, and CSV export of the filtered set.

- People need to find, rank and act on individual records (accounts, orders, tickets)

- More than ~15 rows

## Avoid it when

- MRR: tabular number with a thin inline bar scaled to the column max

- Footer: page x of y, rows per page, prev/next

## Data shape


## Interactions
- Type to search account or owner (debounced)
- Region select and status chips combine as AND filters; counts update
- Click a header to sort (click again to flip); keyboard: headers are buttons
- Chevron expands a row to show plan, seats, last activity and a 12-month MRR sparkline
- Pagination with rows-per-page; filters reset to page 1
- Export CSV downloads exactly the filtered, sorted rows

## Accessibility
- Real <table> with <th scope=col>, aria-sort on the sorted column
- Sort and expand controls are buttons with labels; expanded state via aria-expanded
- Status pills use icon + word
- Live region announces the result count

# Highlight table (heatmap table)

**Category:** Tables · **Tags:** conditional formatting, matrix, crosstab, totals

A region × month crosstab where every cell is shaded on a sequential ramp, with a switch to scale colour across the whole table, within each row, or within each column, plus marginal total bars.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Two categorical dimensions and one measure, and people want both exact numbers and the pattern
- Spotting seasonality per region, or which region leads each month
- Replacing a grid of numbers that nobody reads

## Avoid it when
- One dimension has more than ~20 members (switch to a heatmap without numbers)
- Signed values (use a diverging ramp version)

## Anatomy
- Row headers left, column headers top, both sticky in scroll
- Cells: number centred, tabular figures; fill from the 7-step sequential ramp; text ink switches by fill luminance
- Totals column and row: plain numbers with thin bars, not shaded — they are a different scale
- Scale switch: Whole table / By row / By column
- Crosshair highlight: hovering a cell outlines its row and column headers

## Data shape
```
{ rows: ["Northeast", …], cols: ["Jan", …], values: [[…], …] }
```

## Interactions
- Scale switch re-shades without moving anything
- Hover a cell: tooltip with value, share of row and of column; its row and column headers highlight
- Click a header to sort rows by that month (or columns stay chronological)

## Accessibility
- Real table with scope attributes
- Every value printed — colour is a reading aid, not the data
- Ink colour picked per cell for contrast

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0 … --seq-6`, `--s1`, `--grid`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a highlight table (heatmap crosstab) in one self-contained HTML file. Rows are 6 regions, columns are 12 months, cells hold seeded sales values printed in tabular figures and shaded from a 7-step single-hue sequential ramp, with white or dark text chosen per cell by luminance. Add a Totals column and Totals row shown as plain numbers with thin inline bars (not shaded, since they're a different scale). A segmented control switches colour scaling between Whole table, By row and By column. Hovering a cell shows a tooltip with value, share of its row and share of its column, and highlights its row and column headers. Clicking a month header sorts the rows by that month (click the Region header to reset). Semantic <table> with scope attributes and a small legend of the ramp. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

A three-level tree table (category › sub-category › product) with subtotals, expand/collapse per row or all at once, % of total bars and a profit-margin column that flags losses.

# Scorecard table vs target

**Category:** Tables · **Tags:** balanced scorecard, diverging cells, target, team comparison

Teams × KPIs scorecard where each cell is tinted on a diverging scale by its distance from target (blue = better, red = worse, grey = on target), with an overall score bar and best-in-column markers.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Comparing many units (teams, stores, agents) on several KPIs with targets
- Monthly performance reviews where 'who needs help on what?' is the question
- KPIs have different units and directions, so raw colour scales would mislead

## Avoid it when
- No targets exist (use a highlight table)
- Readers need trend, not position (add sparklines instead)

## Anatomy
- Header row: KPI name, target, and direction hint (↑ better / ↓ better)
- Cells: value centred; fill = diverging tint by normalised gap to target (capped at ±25%), neutral grey within ±2%
- Best value per column gets a 2px ink ring
- Overall score column: mean of capped normalised gaps → 0–100, shown as a bar + number
- Rows sortable by any column

## Data shape
```
{ kpis: [{ key: "csat", name: "CSAT", target: 4.5, better: "up", fmt: "0.0" }, …], rows: [{ team: "Atlanta", csat: 4.6, aht: 312, … }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Click a column header to sort by it (direction-aware: best first)
- Hover a cell: value, target, gap and whether it beats target
- 'Show gaps' toggle swaps values for signed % vs target

## Accessibility
- Values (or gaps) always printed
- Direction of 'better' written in each header
- Best marker is a ring (shape), not colour

## Design tokens used
`--div-neg / --div-mid / --div-pos`, `--ink`, `--s1`, `--track` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a scorecard table in one self-contained HTML file. Rows are 10 teams; columns are 6 KPIs with different units and directions (e.g. CSAT ↑, average handle time ↓, first-contact resolution ↑, abandonment rate ↓, QA score ↑, cost per contact ↓), each with a target shown in the header together with '↑ better' or '↓ better'. Each cell prints the value and is tinted on a diverging red ↔ grey ↔ blue scale by its normalised gap to target (direction-aware, capped at ±25%, grey within ±2%), with text colour chosen by luminance. Ring the best value in each column with a 2px ink outline. Add an Overall column: average of the capped normalised gaps mapped to 0–100, shown as a bar and number. Clicking any header sorts rows best-first by that column. A toggle swaps values for signed % vs target. Hover tooltips show value, target and gap. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

# Ranked bar chart with highlight

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** horizontal bar, top N, other bucket, average line, click to select

Horizontal bars ranked by value with a Top 5 / 10 / All control that folds the rest into 'Other', an average reference line, value labels at the tips and click-to-highlight.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Comparing a measure across categories with long names
- The ranking itself is the insight (top sellers, worst performers)
- You want one item called out against the rest

## Avoid it when
- Categories have a natural order (months, stages) — keep that order and use columns
- Part-to-whole is the point (use a 100% bar or waffle)

## Anatomy
- Label column left (right-aligned text), bars from a single baseline, ≤ 24px thick with 4px rounded tips
- Bars in one hue; highlighted bar in the accent, the rest in de-emphasis grey once something is selected
- 'Other' row last: a text summary (combined total and average) rather than a bar, so the remainder never flattens the scale
- Value label at each bar tip in secondary ink
- Average: 1px ink vertical line with a small 'Avg' label

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Pacific Northwest", value: 1840000 }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Top N control folds the remainder into 'Other'
- Sort: value (desc) or name (A–Z)
- Click a bar to highlight it and show its rank/gap to average in the subtitle; click again to clear
- Hover: tooltip with value, share and rank

## Accessibility
- Bars are focusable buttons-in-SVG with aria-labels; Enter selects
- Values printed at tips
- Highlight uses colour plus a bold label

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--de-emph`, `--ink`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a ranked horizontal bar chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. 18 seeded categories (sales territories). Bars grow from one baseline, max 24px thick with 4px rounded tips and square at the baseline; labels right-aligned in a left column; value labels at the bar tips in secondary ink. Controls: Top 5 / Top 10 / All (fold the remainder into an 'Other' row that always sits last and is shown as text — combined total and average — rather than a bar, so it never flattens the scale) and Sort by value or name. Draw a 1px ink vertical line at the average with a small 'Avg' label. Clicking a bar highlights it in the accent colour and turns the rest de-emphasis grey; the subtitle then states its rank and gap to average; clicking again clears. # Waterfall (bridge) chart

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** P&L, bridge, variance, EBITDA, contributions

A profit-and-loss bridge from revenue to net income: floating bars for each increase or decrease, solid subtotal bars, connector lines between steps and value labels; switch quarters to watch the bridge rebuild.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Explaining how a starting value becomes an ending value through additions and subtractions
- P&L walks, budget-to-actual variance, headcount bridges, price-volume-mix
- The audience is finance or leadership

## Avoid it when
- Steps aren't additive
- There are more than ~12 steps (group minor ones)

## Anatomy
- Columns ≤ 48px with 4px rounding on the free end only
- Increase = diverging positive hue, decrease = diverging negative hue, totals/subtotals = solid ink-2
- 1px dashed connectors from each bar's end to the next bar's start
- Value labels above increases and below decreases (signed), totals labelled in ink weight
- Hairline grid and compact y ticks; category labels wrap to two lines

## Data shape
```
[{ label: "Revenue", value: 4.82e6, type: "total" }, { label: "COGS", value: -1.93e6 }, { label: "Gross profit", type: "subtotal" }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Quarter switch animates bars to new heights
- Hover a bar: start, change and end values, plus % of revenue

## Accessibility
- Every step labelled with a signed value — direction not carried by colour alone
- Legend explains increase / decrease / total
- SVG has an aria-label summarising start and end

## Design tokens used
`--div-pos`, `--div-neg`, `--ink-2`, `--axis`, `--grid` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a P&L waterfall (bridge) chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. Steps: Revenue (total) → COGS → Gross profit (subtotal) → Sales & marketing → R&D → G&A → EBITDA (subtotal) → D&A → Interest → Taxes → Net income (total), with seeded values for four quarters. Draw floating columns (≤48px wide, 4px rounding on the free end only): increases in the diverging positive colour, decreases in the diverging negative colour, totals and subtotals solid in secondary ink, all starting from zero. # Conversion funnel

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** conversion, drop-off, stages, segments, ordinal ramp

A stage-by-stage funnel drawn as aligned horizontal bars on an ordinal blue ramp, with step conversion and drop-off between stages, overall conversion, and a device segment switch.

- A process with ordered stages where people drop out (signup, checkout, hiring, sales pipeline)
- The biggest leak is the insight
- Comparing funnel shape across segments

## Avoid it when
- Stages aren't strictly sequential subsets

## Anatomy
- One row per stage: name + count on the left, bar from a common left baseline, % of first stage at the tip
- Bars on an ordinal ramp (seq step 250 → 700 in light mode) — darker = deeper in the funnel
- Between rows: step conversion '↓ 42% continue' and drop-off count in muted text; the worst step flagged with a ▲ 'Biggest drop' marker
- Header readout: overall conversion first → last

## Data shape
```

```

## Interactions
- Segment switch: All / Mobile / Desktop — bars animate to new widths
- Hover a bar: count, % of start, % of previous stage
- Hover a step connector: drop-off detail

## Accessibility
- All rates printed as text
- Biggest drop marked with a glyph + words
- Ordinal ramp starts at a step that clears 2:1 against the surface

## Design tokens used
`--seq-1 … --seq-6`, `--ink`, `--muted` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt

# Donut with interactive legend

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** donut, part to whole, legend filter, centre readout

A donut chart whose centre shows the total (or the hovered slice), with a legend table that toggles slices on and off and recomputes shares — the polished way to do the pie everyone asks for.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Stakeholders insist on a pie/donut for 2–6 parts of a whole
- One or two parts dominate and that's the message
- The legend doubles as the precise readout

## Avoid it when
- More than 6 parts or similar-sized parts (use a ranked bar)
- Comparing composition across groups (use 100% stacked bars)

## Anatomy
- Ring 20px thick with 2px surface gaps between slices; starts at 12 o'clock, largest first, 'Other' last
- Centre: total (or hovered slice value + name) in ink, label in secondary ink
- Legend table to the right: toggle swatch, name, value, share — tabular numbers
- Hidden slices show a hollow swatch and struck-through name; shares recompute over the visible parts

## Data shape

- Keyboard: legend rows are checkbox-like buttons

## Accessibility
- Legend rows use role=switch with aria-checked
- Every value and share is in the legend text
- Uses categorical slots in fixed order, so colours never shift when slices hide

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s6`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

# Slopegraph

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** before and after, rank change, two periods, highlight

Two vertical axes (before and after) joined by one line per category: biggest riser and faller highlighted by default, everything else grey, hover to spotlight any line, and a Value / Rank switch.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Exactly two time points (or two conditions) per category
- Both the change and the re-ordering matter
- A cleaner alternative to clustered bars for before/after

## Avoid it when
- More than two periods (use a line chart)
- Many categories crossing at similar values (labels collide — use a dumbbell or table)

## Anatomy
- Two labelled period axes at left and right
- Lines 1.5px de-emphasis grey; highlighted lines 2.5px in diverging positive (riser) / negative (faller) hues with 8px end dots + surface ring
- Labels at both ends: name + value; labels nudged apart by a minimum spacing with thin leader ticks so they never overlap
- Value mode uses a shared linear scale; Rank mode uses evenly spaced ranks (1 at top)

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Austin", before: 61.2, after: 74.8 }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Hover a line or label: it turns ink and comes to front; others fade
- Value / Rank switch
- Click a line to pin the highlight

## Accessibility
- Every line labelled at both ends with values
- Riser/faller called out in the subtitle in words
- Highlight uses width and dots, not only colour

## Design tokens used
`--div-pos`, `--div-neg`, `--de-emph`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a slopegraph in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG. 12 seeded cities each with a 2025 and 2026 score. Draw two vertical period axes (left 2025, right 2026) and one line per city; by default all lines are 1.5px de-emphasis grey except the biggest riser (diverging positive colour) and biggest faller (diverging negative colour), drawn 2.5px with 8px end dots that have a 2px surface ring. Label both ends with name and value; resolve label collisions by enforcing a minimum vertical spacing and drawing thin leader ticks from the dot to the moved label. Hovering a line or label turns it ink, brings it to the front and fades the others; clicking pins it. A Value / Rank segmented control switches between a shared linear value scale and evenly spaced ranks. The subtitle names the riser and faller in words. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Dumbbell (gap) chart

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** gap analysis, two values, range, sorted dot plot

One row per category with two dots joined by a bar — this year vs target, or group A vs group B — sortable by gap, current value or name, with the gap printed at the end of each row.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The gap between two values per category is the story (actual vs target, before vs after, men vs women)
- Values don't start at zero, so bars would waste space
- 10–25 categories

## Avoid it when
- Only one value per category (use a bar or dot plot)
- More than two values per row (use a strip plot)

## Anatomy
- Two dots ≥ 8px (series slots 1 and 2) with a 2px surface ring, legend at top
- Connector: 4px rounded bar in a neutral tint between the dots
- Category labels left, gap value right (signed, coloured by whether the gap is good)
- Hairline vertical grid with compact ticks; scale does not need to start at zero

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Engineering", a: 82, b: 76 }, …] — a = this year, b = target (or group A / B)
```

## Interactions
- Sort by gap, by this year, or by name
- Hover a row: both values and the gap; the row gets a wash
- Toggle 'Show only misses' to filter to rows below target

## Accessibility
- Legend present (two series)
- Gap printed as signed text
- Dots differ by colour and the legend; the gap colour follows the up/down text tokens

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--de-emph`, `--up`, `--down`, `--grid` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt

Hairline vertical grid with compact ticks; the axis need not start at zero. Legend at top for the two series. Controls: sort by gap / this year / name, and a 'Misses only' toggle that filters to rows below target. Rows animate when sorted. Hover a row for a tooltip and a hover wash. A true funnel shape: each stage is a slice whose top width is that stage's count and whose curved sides narrow to the next stage, with conversion between stages on the right and a segment switch that morphs the shape.

## Accessibility
- Every count and rate is printed as text
- SVG aria-label lists the stages and counts
- Weakest step marked with ▲ and words, not colour

## Design tokens used
`--seq-1 … --seq-6`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

# Sankey diagram

**Category:** Flows & networks · **Tags:** flow, journey, draggable, attribution, budget

A three-stage Sankey (traffic source → landing page → outcome) with ribbons sized by volume, coloured by source, hover-to-trace highlighting, click-to-pin and vertically draggable nodes.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing how a quantity splits and recombines across 2–4 stages (traffic to outcomes, budget to spend, energy, patient pathways)
- The biggest flows are the story
- Up to ~20 nodes

## Avoid it when
- Flows loop back (cycles) — use a network diagram
- Exact comparison of small flows matters (pair with a table)
- Only one stage of splits (a stacked bar is simpler)

## Anatomy
- Nodes: 12px-wide rounded bars in columns, height ∝ throughput, 10px vertical padding
- Ribbons: cubic Bézier bands whose width ∝ flow, ordered to avoid crossings, 35% opacity in the source node's colour
- First-column nodes use categorical slots in fixed order; later nodes are neutral ink-2
- Labels: name + value beside each node (right of nodes, left of the last column)

## Data shape
```
{ nodes: [{ id: "organic", name: "Organic search", col: 0 }, …], links: [{ source: "organic", target: "home", value: 18200 }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a node: every ribbon through it highlights (65% opacity), others fade to 8%
- Hover a ribbon: tooltip with source → target, value and its share of the source
- Click a node to pin the highlight; click again or Esc to clear
- Drag a node up or down to untangle; ribbons follow

## Accessibility
- SVG aria-label summarises the largest flows
- A 'Table' toggle lists every flow with values
- Ribbon colour carries source identity, and every node is labelled

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--ink-2`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a draggable Sankey diagram in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries (write the layout yourself). Three columns: 5 traffic sources → 4 landing pages → 3 outcomes (Purchase, Sign-up, Bounce), with seeded link values. Layout: node height ∝ max(inflow, outflow) using one global scale, 10px padding between nodes, 12px-wide rounded node bars, columns evenly spaced. Links are filled Bézier ribbons whose width is the flow value, sorted at each node by the other end's vertical position to minimise crossings, coloured by the first-column source (categorical slots in fixed order; downstream ribbons inherit the colour of the traffic that feeds them, so split second-stage links by source) at 35% opacity. Label every node with name and value (to the right, or to the left for the last column). Hovering a node highlights all ribbons through it (others fade to 8%); hovering a ribbon shows source → target, value and share; clicking a node pins the highlight; nodes can be dragged vertically with pointer events and ribbons follow. Add a Diagram / Table toggle. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

# Network (node-link) diagram

**Category:** Flows & networks · **Tags:** force-directed, graph, relationships, collaboration, draggable

A force-directed network of who collaborates with whom: node size = connections, colour = team, link width = interactions; hover to see neighbours, drag nodes, filter by team and search by name.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Relationships are the data: collaboration, service dependencies, referrals, co-purchases
- Finding hubs, bridges between groups and isolated clusters
- Up to ~80 nodes and a few hundred links

## Avoid it when
- Hundreds of nodes (becomes a hairball — aggregate, or use an adjacency matrix)
- Flows have a direction and stages (use a Sankey)

## Anatomy
- Nodes: circles, radius ∝ √degree (5–16px), team colour from the first three categorical slots, 2px surface ring
- Links: 1–4px lines ∝ interaction count, axis-grey at 60% opacity
- Labels only for the top hubs by default; every node labelled on hover/focus
- Team legend chips that double as filters; search box highlights a match
- Side panel: selected person, team, degree and their strongest connections

## Data shape
```
{ nodes: [{ id: "p01", name: "Avery Kim", team: "Engineering" }, …], links: [{ source: "p01", target: "p07", weight: 12 }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a node: it and its neighbours stay full strength, everything else fades; tooltip with degree
- Drag a node to reposition (simulation re-heats briefly)
- Click a node to select it and fill the side panel
- Team chips filter; search jumps to and selects a person
- 'Re-layout' re-runs the simulation

## Accessibility
- Side panel lists the selected node's connections as text
- Search provides a keyboard path to any node
- Team is shown by colour plus legend and panel text; only three categorical slots are used (validated all-pairs)

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--axis`, `--surface`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an interactive force-directed network diagram in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and a hand-written force simulation (no libraries): many-body repulsion, link springs, a weak pull to the centre, collision padding and velocity damping, run with requestAnimationFrame until it cools. Seeded data: ~40 fictional people in 3 teams with ~90 weighted collaboration links, denser within teams and a few cross-team bridges. Node radius ∝ √degree (5–16px), fill = team colour (first three categorical slots), 2px surface ring; links 1–4px ∝ weight in axis grey at 60% opacity. Label only the top 6 hubs by default. Hover highlights a node and its neighbours and fades the rest; drag nodes with pointer events (re-heat the simulation); click selects a node and fills a side panel with name, team, degree and the strongest connections. Team legend chips act as filters, a search box selects a person by name, and a 'Re-layout' button restarts the simulation. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

# Streamgraph

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** stacked area, wiggle, composition over time, 100% area, trends

Six categories as flowing streams over a year, centred on a wavy baseline, with a Stream / Stacked / 100% offset switch, direct labels on the widest part of each stream and a hover crosshair that reads every layer.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing how the mix of several categories rises and falls over time, where overall shape and rhythm matter more than exact values
- Seasonal or event-driven popularity (genres, topics, product lines)
- Editorial or overview panels

## Avoid it when
- Exact values or precise comparison matter (use small multiples or lines)
- More than ~8 categories (fold into 'Other')
- Values can be negative

## Anatomy
- Layers in categorical slot order, largest-total stream in the middle (inside-out ordering) to minimise wiggle
- Smooth curves; a 1px surface-coloured stroke between layers acts as the gap
- Offset modes: Stream (silhouette, centred), Stacked (zero baseline with y axis), 100% (expand, with % axis)
- Direct labels at each stream's widest point when the label fits; legend always present
- Month labels on x; hairline crosshair on hover

## Data shape
```
{ weeks: ["2026-01-04", …52], series: [{ name: "Pop", values: [52 numbers] }, …6] }
```

## Interactions
- Offset switch re-shapes the layers
- Hover: crosshair at the nearest week, hovered layer stays full strength, tooltip lists every layer's value and share (hovered first)
- Click a legend item to isolate that stream; click again to restore

## Accessibility
- Legend present plus direct labels
- Tooltip lists every value as text
- Isolating a stream gives a single, readable shape

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s6`, `--surface`, `--grid`, `--axis` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a streamgraph in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded weekly listening hours for 6 music genres over 52 weeks, each with its own seasonal peak. Order layers inside-out (largest total in the middle), colour with categorical slots 1–6 in fixed order, draw smooth curves (cubic interpolation) and separate layers with a 1px surface-coloured stroke. Offer three offsets in a segmented control: Stream (silhouette: centred on zero), Stacked (zero baseline with a y axis) and 100% (normalised with a percent axis). Put a direct label at each stream's widest point when it fits, plus a clickable legend that isolates one stream. Month labels on x. Hover shows a hairline crosshair at the nearest week, keeps the hovered layer at full opacity while dimming the rest, and a tooltip lists every genre's value and share for that week. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

# Toast notifications

**Category:** UI patterns · **Tags:** toast, snackbar, alert, notification, status, undo

Card-style toasts with a 4px status edge, a filled status icon, a bold title, a one-line message and a close button, in four variants, plus a live stack with position control, auto-dismiss progress, pause on hover and an Undo action.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Confirming a background action finished (export ready, filters saved, data refreshed)
- Short, non-blocking warnings and errors that don't need a decision
- Offering a quick Undo after a destructive action

## Avoid it when
- The message needs a decision or blocks the task (use a dialog)
- Persistent state (a data source is offline) — use an inline banner
- Long messages or more than one action

## Anatomy
- Card: surface background, 8px radius, soft shadow, 4px left edge in the status colour
- Icon: 22px filled circle in the status colour with a white glyph (✓ i ! ✕) — icon and colour together, never colour alone
- Title (semibold 14px) above a one-line message in secondary ink
- Close ×: 28px hit area, muted until hover
- Optional action button (Undo) right-aligned before the close
- Auto-dismiss bar: 2px progress line along the bottom in the status colour

## Data shape
```
toast({ type: "success" | "info" | "warning" | "error", title: "Export ready", message: "sales_q3.csv has been generated.", action?: { label: "Undo", onClick }, duration?: 5000 })
```

## Interactions
- Trigger buttons fire each variant; up to 4 toasts stack, the oldest leaves first
- Position control: top-right, bottom-right, top-centre, bottom-centre
- Auto-dismiss after 5s (errors stay until closed); hovering or focusing the stack pauses every timer
- Close with ×, Esc closes the newest, Undo runs its action and dismisses
- Enter and exit animate (slide + fade, 180ms); instant under prefers-reduced-motion

## Accessibility
- Success/info/warning go to a polite live region (role=status); errors to an assertive one (role=alert)
- Toasts never steal focus; the close button has an aria-label
- Errors don't auto-dismiss, so nobody misses them
- Status colours are the reserved status set and always paired with an icon and a title

## Design tokens used
`--good`, `--s1`, `--warn`, `--crit`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a toast notification system in one self-contained HTML file (no libraries). Toast design: a white surface card with 8px radius, a soft shadow and a 4px left edge in the status colour; a 22px filled circular icon in the status colour with a white glyph (✓ success, i info, ! warning, ✕ error); a semibold title and a one-line secondary-ink message; a muted × close button (28px hit area) on the right; an optional action button such as Undo; and a 2px auto-dismiss progress line along the bottom. Show the four variants statically in a 'Designs' panel, and provide a live demo: buttons that fire each variant, a position control (top-right, bottom-right, top-centre, bottom-centre), a stack of at most 4 (oldest leaves first), 5-second auto-dismiss (errors persist), pause all timers while the stack is hovered or focused, Esc closes the newest, slide-and-fade enter/exit (instant under prefers-reduced-motion). Announce success/info/warning in a polite role=status region and errors in a role=alert region; never move focus. Expose a toast({type,title,message,action,duration}) function. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Slide-out dashboard menu

**Category:** UI patterns · **Tags:** sidebar, navigation, icon rail, drawer, filters, collapsible

A dashboard sidebar that collapses to an icon rail and slides out to a full menu: workspace monogram, page links with an active accent bar, a collapsible Reports group, a filters section that drives the page, and an off-canvas drawer with a scrim on narrow screens.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Multi-page dashboards that need persistent navigation plus a home for global filters
- Users switch between 'focus on the charts' (rail) and 'find my way' (expanded)
- The same dashboard must work on desktop and phone

## Avoid it when
- A single-page dashboard with two or three filters (put them in one row above the charts)
- Fewer than three destinations (use tabs across the top)

## Anatomy
- Header: monogram logo button + workspace name; collapse toggle (⌘/Ctrl + B); in rail mode only the logo shows, centred, and clicking it expands the sidebar
- Nav items: 20px icon + label, 40px rows; active item gets a 3px accent bar on the left and a tinted pill background
- Collapsible group (Reports) with a chevron and indented children
- Filters section: a period segmented control and region checkboxes with counts, plus a one-line plain-English summary of what's applied
- Footer: user avatar + name and a help link
- Rail mode: 64px wide, icons only, labels in tooltips; expanded: 248px; drawer (narrow screens): slides over content with a 40% scrim
- Two skins from the library: Neutral (hairline, shadcn-like) and Navy (dark rail, GA4/Data Forge-like)

## Data shape
```
{ workspace: "Northstar Retail", pages: [{ id: "overview", label: "Overview", icon: "grid" }, …], groups: [{ label: "Reports", items: […] }], filters: { period: ["7D","30D","QTD","YTD"], regions: [{ name: "West", count: 12 }, …] } }
```

## Interactions
- Collapse/expand with the toggle button or Ctrl/⌘ + B; clicking the logo re-expands a collapsed rail; the choice is remembered per viewer
- Collapse style switch: Collapse to rail (64px icons) or Hide completely (0px; a hamburger in the top bar brings it back, also on desktop)
- Hover a rail icon: tooltip with the page name
- Click a page: active state moves and the content header updates
- Reports group expands/collapses (aria-expanded)
- Filters update the page summary immediately; Reset clears them
- Narrow screens: hamburger opens a drawer; Esc, scrim click or choosing a page closes it; focus is trapped inside while open and returns to the hamburger

## Accessibility
- <nav aria-label> landmark; active link has aria-current=page
- Toggle buttons expose aria-expanded and aria-controls
- Drawer is a modal dialog while open (focus trap, Esc to close, focus restored)
- Rail icons keep accessible names even when labels are hidden
- Visible focus rings; respects prefers-reduced-motion

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--grid`, `--hover` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a responsive slide-out dashboard sidebar in one self-contained HTML file (no libraries), shown inside a mock dashboard frame. Sidebar contents: a header with a monogram tile, workspace name and a collapse toggle (also Ctrl/⌘+B); a nav list of pages with inline SVG icons (Overview, Sales, Customers, Inventory) where the active item has a 3px accent bar on the left, a tinted pill background and aria-current=page; a collapsible 'Reports' group with a chevron and indented children; a Filters section with a period segmented control (7D/30D/QTD/YTD), region checkboxes with counts and a Reset link; and a footer with a user avatar and name. Modes: expanded (248px) and a collapsed state that is either an icon rail (64px, labels hidden but kept as accessible names and shown as hover tooltips, the monogram logo centred and clickable to expand again) or hidden completely (0px wide and inert, with a hamburger in the top bar to bring it back) — chosen with a 'Collapse to rail / Hide completely' switch, animated with a width transition, with the choice remembered in localStorage. Below 720px the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer opened by a hamburger, sliding over the content with a 40% scrim; Esc, scrim click or picking a page closes it, focus is trapped while open and returned to the hamburger. Selecting a page or changing filters updates the content header and a plain-English summary ('Sales · last 30 days · West, South'). Offer two skins via a switch: Neutral (light surface, hairline border) and Navy (dark navy rail with white text). CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes, prefers-reduced-motion respected.

# Bump chart

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** ranking, rank over time, leaderboard history, highlight

Rank over time for ten apps across twelve weeks: smooth lines between rank positions, everything grey except up to three picked apps in colour with rank numbers at every point, and labels at both ends.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The order matters more than the values (charts positions, league tables, market share rank)
- You want to show climbers, fallers and swaps across many periods
- 5–15 entities

## Avoid it when
- The gaps between values matter (a #1 that leads by 40% looks the same as one that leads by 1%) — use a line chart
- Only two periods (use a slopegraph)

## Anatomy
- y = rank (1 at the top), evenly spaced; x = periods
- Lines: smooth S-curves with flat tangents at each period, 2px de-emphasis grey; selected lines 3px in categorical slots 1–3
- Points: 4px grey dots; selected lines get 20px circles with the rank number inside
- Labels at the start (left) and end (right): rank and name; selected labels in ink weight
- Legend chips for the current selection with a clear button

## Data shape
```
{ periods: ["W1", …12], series: [{ name: "Lumen Notes", ranks: [3, 2, 2, 1, …] }, …10] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a line or label: it darkens and a tooltip summarises best, worst and net change
- Click a line or label to add or remove it from the selection (max 3; the oldest drops off)
- Selection keeps its colour while selected — colour follows the app, never its rank

## Accessibility
- Rank numbers printed inside selected points
- Labels at both ends name every line
- SVG aria-label summarises the biggest climber and faller

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--de-emph`, `--ink`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an interactive bump chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded weekly rankings for 10 fictional apps over 12 weeks (derive ranks from noisy scores so lines cross). y is rank with 1 at the top, evenly spaced; x is weeks. Draw each app as a smooth line using cubic curves with horizontal tangents at every week; unselected lines are 2px de-emphasis grey with 4px dots, selected lines (up to 3) are 3px in categorical slots 1–3 with 20px circles that show the rank number in white. Label every line at the left (start rank + name) and right (end rank + name). Hover darkens a line and shows best rank, worst rank and net change; clicking a line or label toggles it in the selection (max 3, oldest drops off), and colours stay attached to the app while selected. Show the selection as legend chips with a Clear button. Default selection: the biggest climber, the biggest faller and the final #1. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Beeswarm

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** distribution, dot plot, individuals, salary bands, jitter-free

Every employee as a dot along a salary axis, swarmed so no dot overlaps, one row per department with a median tick, coloured by level, with level filters and an All-together view.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- You want the distribution and the individuals at once (salaries, response times, deal sizes, scores)
- Comparing distributions across a few groups
- Up to a few hundred points per row

## Avoid it when
- Thousands of points (use a histogram or violin)
- Only the summary matters (a box plot or bar of medians is faster to read)

## Anatomy
- x = value on a shared linear axis with compact ticks and hairline grid
- One swarm per group; dots (r = 4) are placed outward from the row's centre line so none overlap
- Colour = level (categorical slots 1–3, validated all-pairs) with a legend
- Median: a 2px ink tick across each swarm with its value
- Group labels with counts on the left

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Employee 104", department: "Engineering", level: "Manager", salary: 148000 }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Layout switch: By department / All together (re-swarms)
- Level chips filter (dim) levels
- Hover a dot: person, department, level, salary and percentile within the department

## Accessibility
- Medians printed as text
- Level shown by colour plus legend and tooltip; dimming instead of removal keeps the shape
- SVG aria-label gives each department's median

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--ink`, `--grid`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a beeswarm chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded data: ~260 fictional employees in 5 departments and 3 levels (Individual contributor, Manager, Director) with salaries that differ by department and level. Shared x axis for salary with compact ticks and a hairline grid. One row per department: place each dot (radius 4, 1px surface ring) on the x position of its value, then swarm it vertically by trying offsets 0, +d, −d, +2d, … until it doesn't overlap any already-placed dot (process dots sorted by value). Colour by level using the first three categorical slots, with a legend whose chips dim a level when toggled. Draw each department's median as a 2px ink tick with a label, and department names with counts on the left. A segmented control switches between By department and All together. Hover tooltips show name, department, level, salary and percentile within the department. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.
