# Chord diagram

**Category:** Flows & networks · **Tags:** flows between groups, switching, migration, matrix, net gain

Customer switching between five brands drawn as a chord diagram: arc length = customers lost, ribbon ends sized by flow in each direction and coloured by the brand that wins the exchange, with net gain/loss on hover and a matrix view.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Flows between members of the same set go both ways (brand switching, migration between regions, transfers between teams)
- Net winners and losers are the story
- 4–8 groups

## Avoid it when
- Flows go through stages (use a Sankey)
- More than ~8 groups or many tiny flows (use a heatmap matrix)
- Exact comparison of flows (pair with the matrix view)

## Anatomy
- Outer arcs: one per group, 14px thick, length ∝ customers that left the group, 0.04 rad padding, categorical slots in fixed order
- Ribbons: each pair drawn once; each end's width ∝ the flow leaving that side; coloured by the side that gained more, at 65% opacity
- Labels outside each arc with the group name and its net change (signed)
- Matrix view: from × to table with row and column totals

## Data shape
```
{ groups: ["Aurora", "Bramble", …], matrix: [[0, 420, 180, …], …] } — matrix[i][j] = customers who moved from i to j
```

## Interactions
- Hover an arc: its ribbons stay, the rest fade; tooltip with lost, gained and net
- Hover a ribbon: 'A → B 420 · B → A 180 · net +240 to A'
- Click an arc to pin the highlight
- Diagram / Matrix toggle

## Accessibility
- Net change written in every label
- Matrix view carries every number
- Ribbon colour is explained in the subtitle and tooltip

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a chord diagram in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries (compute the layout yourself). Seeded 5×5 brand-switching matrix where matrix[i][j] is customers who moved from brand i to brand j (diagonal zero). Lay out one outer arc per brand around a circle, arc length proportional to the row total (customers lost), with 0.04 radian padding, 14px thick, coloured by categorical slots 1–5 in fixed order. Inside each arc, sub-divide by destination; draw each pair once as a ribbon from the i→j sub-arc to the j→i sub-arc with quadratic curves through the centre, coloured by the brand that gained more from the exchange, at 65% opacity. Label each arc outside the circle with the brand name and its signed net change. Hovering an arc keeps its ribbons and fades others (tooltip: lost, gained, net); hovering a ribbon shows both directions and the net; clicking an arc pins it. Add a Diagram / Matrix toggle that shows the from × to table with totals. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Radar chart

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** spider chart, profile comparison, multivariate, benchmark

Product profiles across seven scored attributes on a shared 0–100 scale: up to three products as outlined polygons with light fills, an industry benchmark as a dashed ink outline, toggleable legend and per-vertex tooltips, plus a table view.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Comparing the shape of 2–3 profiles across 5–8 attributes on the same scale (product reviews, skills, vendor scorecards)
- Showing strengths and gaps at a glance
- The audience is used to spider charts

## Avoid it when
- Attributes have different units or scales (normalise first or use bullet charts)
- Precise comparison per attribute (use grouped bars or a dot plot — area exaggerates differences)
- More than three series (shapes become unreadable)

## Anatomy
- Spokes: one per attribute, axis-grey; rings every 20 points in hairline grid with small value labels on the first spoke
- Series polygons: 2px outline in categorical slots 1–3, 12% fill, 8px vertex dots with surface rings
- Benchmark: 1.5px dashed ink outline, no fill
- Attribute labels outside the rim, anchored by side
- Legend with toggles; a single hover highlights one series and fades the others

## Data shape
```
{ axes: ["Ease of use", "Speed", …7], series: [{ name: "Product A", values: [82, 64, …] }, …3], benchmark: [70, 70, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Click legend items to show/hide a series (at least one stays)
- Hover a polygon or legend item to bring that series forward
- Hover a vertex: attribute, value and difference from benchmark
- Chart / Table toggle

## Accessibility
- Legend present (≥ 2 series); benchmark distinguished by dash, not colour
- Table view lists every value
- Uses only the three categorical slots validated for overlapping shapes

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--ink`, `--grid`, `--axis`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an interactive radar (spider) chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seven attributes scored 0–100 for three fictional products plus an industry benchmark. Draw spokes in axis grey, concentric polygon rings every 20 points in hairline grid with small value labels along the first spoke, and attribute labels outside the rim anchored left/right/middle by angle. Each product is a polygon with a 2px outline in categorical slots 1–3, a 12% fill and 8px vertex dots with a 2px surface ring; the benchmark is a 1.5px dashed ink outline with no fill. Legend items toggle series (never hide the last) and hovering a legend item or polygon brings it to the front and fades the others. Vertex hover shows the attribute, value and difference from benchmark. Add a Chart / Table toggle. CSS variables for all colours, light and dark themes.

# Collapsible tree diagram

**Category:** Hierarchies · **Tags:** org chart, hierarchy, dendrogram, tidy tree, drill down

A left-to-right tidy tree of an organisation (company › departments › teams › squads): node size = headcount, branches coloured by department, click any node to expand or collapse it, with expand-all, collapse-all and a search that opens the path to a match.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing structure and size of a hierarchy together (org charts, product taxonomies, account hierarchies, decision trees)
- Readers explore by drilling into one branch
- Up to ~200 nodes with a few expanded at a time

## Avoid it when
- Part-to-whole proportion is the point (use a treemap)
- The structure is a network with cross-links (use a node-link diagram)

## Anatomy
- Columns by depth, rows by visible leaves; parents centred on their children
- Links: smooth horizontal S-curves from parent to child, 1.5px in the branch colour at 45% opacity
- Nodes: circles with radius ∝ √headcount; filled when collapsed (has hidden children), ring when expanded, small dot for leaves
- Labels to the right of each node: name and headcount; the root and departments in ink weight
- Department colours: categorical slots 1–5, inherited down the branch

## Data shape
```
{ name: "Northstar Retail", children: [{ name: "Engineering", children: [{ name: "Platform", size: 42 }, …] }, …] } — internal sizes are summed
```

## Interactions
- Click (or Enter) a node with children to expand/collapse it
- Expand all / Collapse to departments buttons
- Search: type a team name to expand the path and outline the match
- Hover: tooltip with headcount, share of the parent and of the company

## Accessibility
- role=tree with treeitem nodes, aria-level and aria-expanded
- Every node is focusable and togglable with Enter/Space
- Headcount printed beside every node

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a collapsible tidy tree in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded org data: company → 5 departments → 3–5 teams → 2–4 squads with headcounts at the leaves (parents summed). Layout left to right: x by depth, y by visible-leaf order with 26px rows, each parent centred on its visible children; the SVG height follows the number of visible leaves. Links are horizontal S-curves (cubic Béziers) in the branch's department colour at 45% opacity; departments take categorical slots 1–5 and children inherit them. Node circles have radius ∝ √headcount, filled when collapsed with hidden children, a ring when expanded, and a small dot for leaves; labels to the right show name and headcount. Clicking a node or pressing Enter toggles it; add Expand all and Collapse buttons and a search box that expands the path to a matching team and outlines it. Use role=tree / treeitem with aria-level and aria-expanded. Tooltips show headcount and shares. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Voronoi treemap

**Category:** Hierarchies · **Tags:** treemap, weighted voronoi, power diagram, part to whole, hierarchy, zoom

A two-level hierarchy (category › product line) packed into a circle as organic Voronoi cells whose areas match their values; click a category to zoom in and re-pack its lines to fill the circle.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing part-to-whole for a two-level hierarchy with a memorable, organic look (budgets, revenue mix, market share)
- Editorial or hero panels where a rectangular treemap feels too rigid
- Up to ~40 leaf cells

## Avoid it when
- Precise comparison of similar values (areas of irregular shapes are hard to compare — use bars)
- Deep hierarchies (beyond two levels, use a tree diagram or a zoomable rectangular treemap)
- Data that updates often (the layout is iterative and positions move)

## Anatomy
- Boundary: a circle; top-level cells are a weighted Voronoi (power) diagram whose areas converge to each category's share
- Second level: each category cell is subdivided the same way for its product lines
- Category colours: categorical slots 1–5; lines are tints of their category's hue
- Borders: 4px surface lines between categories, 1.5px between lines
- Labels: category name + share at each category's centroid (overview); line name + value inside cells large enough (zoomed)
- Side list: categories with value and share, doubling as zoom buttons

## Data shape
```
{ name: "Revenue", children: [{ name: "Electronics", children: [{ name: "Phones", value: 32 }, …] }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Click a category (cell or side list) to zoom in; Back or Esc to return
- Hover a cell: tooltip with value, share of category and of total
- Layout is computed once per view (deterministic seed) and reused on resize

## Accessibility
- Side list gives every category value and share as text and acts as keyboard-accessible zoom buttons
- Zoomed view labels every line large enough to hold text; the rest are in tooltips and the list
- SVG aria-label lists the categories with shares

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--surface`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a two-level Voronoi treemap in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Implement a weighted Voronoi (power diagram) layout yourself: each cell is the boundary polygon clipped by the half-planes 2(pj−pi)·x ≤ |pj|²−|pi|²−wj+wi for every other site j (Sutherland–Hodgman clipping). Iterate ~150 times: compute cells, move each site to its cell centroid, scale its weight by target area ÷ current area, cap each weight at the squared distance to its nearest neighbour site, and reset any empty cell. Seed sites deterministically inside the boundary. Use a circle (72-gon) as the top boundary for 5 categories, then subdivide each category cell for its 3–5 product lines. Colour categories with categorical slots 1–5 and lines as lighter tints of their category; separate categories with 4px surface-coloured borders and lines with 1.5px borders. Overview labels show category name and share at each centroid with a surface halo. Clicking a category (or its entry in a side list) zooms: re-pack its lines to fill the whole circle with name and value labels; Back or Esc returns. Hover tooltips show value and shares. Compute layouts in a fixed 500×500 space and scale via viewBox so resizing doesn't re-run them. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Area bump chart

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** ranked stream, rank and size, market share, ribbons

A bump chart whose lines are ribbons: at each quarter the services are stacked in rank order, ribbon thickness is their share, and smooth crossovers show overtakes, with direct labels and hover focus.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Both rank and size matter over time (market share, watch time, votes)
- Overtakes are the story but you don't want to hide how big the gaps are
- 5–8 series over 6–20 periods

## Avoid it when
- Only rank matters (a plain bump chart is cleaner)
- Exact values must be compared (use lines or small multiples)
- Many series with similar sizes (ribbons become a tangle)

## Anatomy
- At each period, series stack top to bottom by rank with a 6px gap; thickness ∝ value
- Between periods, each ribbon's edges follow cubic curves with horizontal tangents, so swaps read as crossovers
- Categorical slots in fixed order per series; 1px surface stroke separates overlapping ribbons
- Direct labels at the right edge (name + share) and left edge (name), placed in each ribbon's middle
- Period labels along the bottom; hover crosshair

## Data shape
```
{ periods: ["Q1 '24", …], series: [{ name: "Streamly", values: [ …share per period ] }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a ribbon: it stays full strength, others fade to 20%; tooltip with rank and share at the hovered period
- Click a ribbon to pin the focus; click again to clear
- Metric switch: Share of watch time / Hours

## Accessibility
- Every ribbon is labelled at both ends, so colour is not the only identifier
- Tooltip lists rank and value as text
- SVG aria-label names the current leader and the biggest climber

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s6`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--grid` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an area bump chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded quarterly data for 6 fictional streaming services over 10 quarters (share of watch time, with a couple of overtakes). At each quarter, sort services by value and stack them top to bottom with a 6px gap so each ribbon's thickness is proportional to its value and its vertical position is its rank. Between quarters, draw each ribbon's top and bottom edges as cubic Bézier curves with horizontal tangents so rank swaps become smooth crossovers; fill with categorical slots 1–6 in fixed per-service order and a 1px surface-coloured stroke. Label every ribbon at the right edge (name + latest share) and at the left edge (name), centred in the ribbon. Hovering a ribbon fades the others to 20% and shows a tooltip with its rank and value at the hovered quarter; clicking pins the focus. Add a metric switch between share and absolute hours. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Polar area (Nightingale rose)

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** coxcomb, rose chart, seasonality, cyclical, stacked

Twelve monthly wedges whose area (not radius) is proportional to value, stacked by cause like Nightingale's rose, with a stacked / single-cause switch, square-root rings and hover readouts.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Cyclical data where the circle itself means something (months, hours, compass directions)
- Showing seasonality in a striking, editorial way
- 2–3 stacked components

## Avoid it when
- Precise comparison between non-adjacent wedges (use a bar chart)
- Linear time without a cycle
- More than three stacked components (outer layers get distorted)

## Anatomy
- 12 equal-angle wedges starting at 12 o'clock with 1.5px surface gaps
- Radius = √(cumulative value) so each layer's area is proportional to its value (never linear radius — that squares the differences)
- Stacked layers in categorical slots 1–3, innermost first; legend above
- Reference rings at round values on the square-root scale, labelled along the top spoke
- Month labels outside the rim

## Data shape
```
[{ month: "Jan", causes: { Preventable: 42, Wounds: 12, Other: 8 } }, …12]
```

## Interactions
- Switch: All causes (stacked) or one cause at a time
- Hover a wedge: month, cause, value and share of that month
- Hover a legend item to highlight that layer

## Accessibility
- Legend present; values in tooltips and in a Table view
- Area-true scaling noted in the subtitle
- Only the three categorical slots validated for all-pairs use

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--grid`, `--surface`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a polar area (Nightingale rose / coxcomb) chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Twelve monthly wedges of equal angle starting at 12 o'clock with 1.5px surface-coloured gaps, each stacked from three seeded components (e.g. incident causes). Make AREA proportional to value: the outer radius of each stacked layer is r = R × √(cumulative value ÷ max monthly total). Fill layers with categorical slots 1–3, innermost first. Draw reference rings at round values on the same square-root scale with labels on the top spoke, and month labels outside the rim. A segmented control switches between All causes (stacked) and each single cause (rescaled to its own max). Hovering a wedge shows month, cause, value and share of the month; hovering a legend item highlights that layer. Include a Table toggle. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Radial Sankey

**Category:** Flows & networks · **Tags:** sunburst flow, budget allocation, hierarchy flow, circular sankey

A budget flowing outward from a centre total through departments to programmes: concentric rings of arcs with curved bands fanning between them, coloured by department, with hover tracing and a list view.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- A total splits into categories and then sub-categories and you want the split to feel like a flow (budgets, revenue allocation, headcount plans)
- Hero or summary panels where a sunburst feels too static
- 2 levels, up to ~30 outer items

## Avoid it when
- Flows recombine or cross between branches (use a regular Sankey)
- Precise value comparison (pair with the list view or bars)
- Deep hierarchies (beyond two levels the outer ring gets crowded)

## Anatomy
- Centre: total value and label
- Ring 1: department arcs (angle ∝ value), 14px thick, categorical slots 1–5
- Ring 2: programme arcs spread with extra padding so the bands fan out, 14px thick, tints of the department hue
- Bands: curved ribbons from each department's arc segment to each programme's arc, 45% opacity
- Labels: department names along ring 1 (outside when they fit), programme names radially outside ring 2

## Data shape
```
{ total: "FY2027 budget", children: [{ name: "Engineering", children: [{ name: "Platform", value: 18.4 }, …] }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Hover a department or programme: its branch stays, the rest fade; tooltip with value and shares
- Click a department to pin its branch
- Chart / List toggle

## Accessibility
- List view gives every value with its department
- Centre total in text; tooltips state shares
- Department labels name every colour

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s5`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a radial Sankey in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded two-level budget: 5 departments, each with 3–5 programmes. In the centre, print the total. Ring 1 (inner) holds department arcs whose angles are proportional to value, 14px thick, in categorical slots 1–5 with small angular padding. Ring 2 (outer, at a larger radius) holds programme arcs, also proportional to value but with larger padding so they fan out, coloured as lighter tints of their department. Connect each programme to its department's arc segment with a curved band: start at the department ring's outer edge across the programme's share of that arc, end at the programme arc's inner edge, using cubic curves through a mid radius, at 45% opacity. Label departments near ring 1 and programmes radially outside ring 2, rotated to read outward and flipped on the left half. Hover highlights a whole branch and shows a tooltip; clicking a department pins it. Add a Chart / List toggle. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Ternary plot

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** three-part composition, simplex, channel mix, barycentric, change arrows

Each store's sales mix across three channels (online, in-store, wholesale) as a point in a triangle, sized by revenue and coloured by format, with guide lines to the three axes on hover and arrows showing how the mix moved since last year.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Every item is a mix of exactly three parts that sum to 100% (channel mix, soil texture, time allocation, vote shares)
- Clusters and drift in composition are the story
- 10–200 items

## Avoid it when
- More or fewer than three parts
- Readers are unfamiliar with the form and there's no room to explain it (use 100% stacked bars)
- Absolute amounts matter more than proportions

## Anatomy
- Equilateral triangle; each corner is 100% of one part, the opposite edge is 0%
- Grid lines every 20% parallel to each edge, ticks labelled on one edge per axis, in hairline grid
- Points: circles sized by revenue (√), coloured by store format (categorical slots 1–3), 2px surface ring
- Hover: dashed guide lines from the point to all three axes with the three percentages
- Change mode: thin arrows from last year's mix to this year's

## Data shape
```
[{ store: "Store 12", format: "Urban", revenue: 4.2e6, mix: { online: .38, inStore: .52, wholesale: .10 }, mixLastYear: { … } }, …]
```

## Interactions
- Toggle: This year / Change since last year (arrows)
- Format chips dim other formats
- Hover a point: guides to each axis and a tooltip with the three shares and revenue

## Accessibility
- Corner labels and an axis explainer in the subtitle
- Tooltip states all three percentages in words
- Only three categorical slots, validated all-pairs

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--grid`, `--axis`, `--ink`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an interactive ternary plot in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded data: 36 fictional stores in 3 formats (Urban, Suburban, Outlet), each with revenue and a sales mix across Online / In-store / Wholesale for this year and last year (each mix sums to 1). Draw an equilateral triangle with Online at the top, In-store bottom-left and Wholesale bottom-right; add grid lines every 20% parallel to each edge in hairline grid with tick labels along one edge per axis and corner labels. Convert each mix to x,y with barycentric coordinates. Points are circles sized by √revenue, coloured by format (categorical slots 1–3) with a 2px surface ring. Hovering a point draws dashed guide lines from it to each axis and shows a tooltip with the three shares and revenue. A toggle switches to 'Change since last year', drawing thin arrows from last year's position to this year's. Format chips dim other formats. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Globe with flight paths

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** orthographic, great circle, routes, 3D globe, draggable, canvas

A dotted orthographic globe with great-circle routes arcing out of a hub: route width = passengers, animated travellers along each path, drag to spin, auto-rotate, and a ranked route list that flies the globe to any destination.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Origin–destination data across continents (flights, shipping lanes, data-centre traffic, customer reach)

## Avoid it when

- Low-power or print contexts (use a static flat map with arcs)

## Anatomy
- Orthographic projection on canvas; sphere in a surface tint with an axis-grey rim and a faint 30° graticule
- Land as a dot matrix (every ~2.4°), dots fade towards the limb for depth
- Routes: great-circle arcs lifted above the surface in the middle, width 1–3.5px ∝ passengers, accent colour; hidden where they pass behind the globe
- Moving travellers: small dots running along each route (off under prefers-reduced-motion)
- Hub: ink dot with a surface ring and label; destinations: accent dots
- Side list: routes ranked by passengers with bars; selecting one flies the globe to it

## Data shape
```
{ hub: { name: "Chicago", lat: 41.98, lon: -87.9 }, routes: [{ to: "London", lat: 51.47, lon: -0.45, passengers: 412000 }, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Drag to rotate (pointer events, works with touch)
- Auto-rotate toggle (off by default under prefers-reduced-motion)
- Hover a route: it turns to the second accent and a tooltip shows destination, passengers and distance
- Click a route in the list (or Enter) to fly the globe to it and highlight it

## Accessibility
- The route list carries every value as text and is keyboard operable
- Canvas has a role=img label summarising the hub and top routes
- Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--surface-2`, `--axis`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--grid` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt

Use an orthographic projection with rotation (λ0, φ0): rotate each unit vector about the z axis by −λ0, tilt about the y axis by φ0, draw points with x > 0 (facing the viewer). Draw the sphere in a surface tint with an axis-grey rim and a faint 30° graticule, and land as a dot matrix generated by testing a ~2.4° lat/lon grid against simplified continent polygons (point-in-polygon), fading dots toward the limb. # Curved line chart

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** smooth line, monotone, spline, step, moving average

Daily sessions as faint raw points with a smoothed 7-day average on top, and a curve switch between monotone (no overshoot), natural spline and step interpolation, so you can see how each curve treats the same data.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The trend matters more than each point and a gentle curve reads calmer than zig-zags
- Noisy daily data where a rolling average tells the story
- Step curves for values that change at moments (prices, plan tiers, headcount)

## Avoid it when
- Few points (curves imply data between them that doesn't exist)
- Exact values at each point matter more than the shape
- Natural splines on data near zero or bounded values (they overshoot)

## Anatomy
- Raw daily values: 1.5px line in de-emphasis grey with no markers
- 7-day average: 2.5px accent curve
- Curve options: Monotone (Fritsch–Carlson; never overshoots the data), Natural (Catmull–Rom style; may overshoot), Step (holds each value until the next)
- Weekend bands as faint tints behind the plot
- Legend for both series; crosshair tooltip with raw and average

## Data shape
```
{ days: ["2026-08-26", …60], sessions: [60 numbers] } — the average is computed on the page
```

## Interactions
- Curve switch: Monotone / Natural / Step
- Show raw data on/off
- Hover: crosshair with the day, raw sessions and the 7-day average

## Accessibility
- Legend for both series; the average is also in the tooltip
- Weekend bands are context only, not data
- SVG aria-label states the latest average

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--de-emph`, `--surface-2`, `--grid`, `--axis` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a curved line chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded daily website sessions for 60 days with weekly seasonality (weekend dips) and noise. Draw the raw daily series as a 1.5px de-emphasis grey line and a 7-day rolling average as a 2.5px accent curve. Add a curve-type segmented control: Monotone (implement Fritsch–Carlson monotone cubic interpolation so the curve never overshoots), Natural (Catmull–Rom style cubic through the points) and Step (step-after). # Area chart

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** area, volume over time, target line, date range, gradient

A single-series area chart for a volume measure: accent line over a soft fill anchored at zero, a dashed target line with a label, a date-range switch, and a crosshair that reports the value and the gap to target.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- One cumulative or volume-like measure over time where the filled mass helps (revenue, users, storage)
- You want a hero trend with more presence than a bare line
- Comparing against a single reference value

## Avoid it when
- Several overlapping series (fills hide each other — use lines or a stacked area)
- Values can be negative or the axis can't start at zero (an area implies a zero baseline)

## Anatomy
- 2px accent line with a fill from the line down to zero; fill is a vertical gradient from 22% to 2% opacity
- Always a zero baseline in axis grey
- Target: 1.5px dashed ink line with a right-aligned label
- Hairline grid, compact y ticks, adaptive x labels
- End dot with a surface ring and the latest value labelled

## Data shape
```
{ dates: ["2026-01-01", …], values: [daily numbers], target: 52000 }
```

## Interactions
- Range switch: 1M / 3M / 6M / YTD
- Hover: crosshair, value and difference from target

## Accessibility
- Single series, so the title names it (no legend box needed)
- Latest value and target printed as text
- SVG aria-label states the latest value vs target

## Design tokens used

# Stacked area chart

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** stacked area, 100% area, composition over time, part to whole

Four product lines stacked over twelve months with a Stacked / 100% switch, straight or smooth edges, a legend that toggles layers, and a crosshair tooltip with every layer, its share and the total.

- Stacked: y axis in units from zero; 100%: y axis 0–100%
- Legend toggles layers (colours never shift when a layer hides)
- Crosshair: hairline + tooltip listing layers top-down with value, share and the total

## Data shape


## Interactions
- Mode: Stacked / 100%
- Edges: Straight / Smooth
- Click legend items to hide/show layers (one always stays)
- Hover for the crosshair tooltip

## Accessibility
- Legend present; tooltip lists every value and share
- Colour follows the layer, never its position
- SVG aria-label summarises the latest mix

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s4`, `--surface`, `--grid`, `--axis` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

Add segmented controls for Stacked vs 100% (normalise each month) and Straight vs Smooth edges (cubic interpolation of both the top and bottom of each layer). The y axis starts at zero with compact ticks (or 0–100% in 100% mode), hairline gridlines and month labels. A legend toggles layers on and off without recolouring the rest (never hide the last). # Vertical bar (column) chart

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** column, bar, negative values, target line, highlight

Monthly profit as columns that grow up from zero for gains and down for losses, with rounded data ends, an optional target line, best/worst highlighting and value labels on demand.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Comparing a measure across ordered categories, especially time periods (months, quarters)
- Values can be negative and the sign matters
- Up to ~24 columns

## Avoid it when
- Long category names (use horizontal bars)
- Continuous time with many points (use a line)
- Part-to-whole (use stacked bars or a waffle)

## Anatomy
- Columns ≤ 24px wide, single hue; 4px rounded data end, square at the zero baseline
- Negative columns grow downward in the diverging negative hue; the zero line is axis grey and heavier than the grid
- Highlight mode: best and worst months keep their colour and get labels, the rest go de-emphasis grey
- Optional target: 1.5px dashed ink line with label
- Value labels: off, all (on the cap), or highlights only

## Data shape
```
{ labels: ["Jan", …12], values: [41200, -8300, …] }
```

## Interactions
- Labels: None / All / Best & worst
- Target line on/off
- Hover a column: value and change vs previous month

## Accessibility
- Single series — the title names it
- Negative values carry a minus sign in labels and tooltips, not just colour
- SVG aria-label names the best and worst months

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--div-neg`, `--de-emph`, `--axis`, `--grid`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a column (vertical bar) chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded monthly profit for 12 months including two loss months. Columns are at most 24px wide in the accent colour with a 4px rounded data end and a square end at the zero baseline; negative columns grow downward in the diverging negative colour. The zero line is a heavier axis-grey line; other gridlines are hairline. Controls: value labels None / All / Best & worst (in the last mode, the best and worst months keep their colour and get labels while others turn de-emphasis grey), and a Target line toggle (dashed ink line with a label). Hover tooltips show the value and the change vs the previous month. Labels sit on the column cap (above positives, below negatives). CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Speedometer gauge (configurable)

**Category:** Gauges · **Tags:** speedometer, banded gauge, segmented gauge, tapered needle, target

A bold speedometer: a thick arc that sweeps 180–270°, three gauge styles (banded zones, progress fill, lit segments), a tapered needle with a round hub, an optional target notch and the value set large in the gauge's opening.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- One headline KPI against a range or target, where the dial itself is the hero of the panel
- Executive summaries and wallboards that need an at-a-glance 'how close are we?'
- Ranges with meaningful zones (poor / fair / good)

## Avoid it when
- Comparing several metrics precisely (use bullet charts)
- The trend matters more than the current value (use a KPI card with sparkline)
- Small spaces — the thick arc needs ~220px to read

## Anatomy
- Arc: thick annular band (inner radius ≈ 56% of outer), sweep 180° / 240° / 270°, opening at the bottom
- Banded style: three zones in an ordinal single-hue ramp (light → dark), no gaps between zones
- Progress style: pale track of the same hue with the accent filled from the start to the value
- Segmented style: 12 segments with small gaps; segments up to the value light up along the ramp, the rest stay track-coloured
- Needle: tapered triangle from the hub to the inner edge of the band, ink colour, with a round hub; or a thin line; or none
- Target: an ink notch across the band with a small label outside the arc
- Value: 44px bold in the opening (or under the hub for 180°) with a caption in secondary ink; min and max at the arc ends

## Data shape
```
{ value: 71.6, min: 0, max: 100, target: 80, bands: [50, 80], label: "Progress to target", format: "%" }
```

## Interactions
- Style: Banded / Progress / Segmented
- Sweep: 180° / 240° / 270°
- Needle: Tapered / Line / None
- Target on/off
- Value slider animates the needle and fill (400ms ease-out; instant under prefers-reduced-motion)
- Hover: value, target gap and which zone the value is in

## Accessibility
- role=meter with aria-valuemin / max / now and a text label
- The value and zone are printed, never implied by colour alone
- The slider is a labelled native range input
- Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0 … --seq-6`, `--track`, `--s1`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a configurable speedometer gauge in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries, in a bold modern style: a thick annular arc (inner radius about 56% of the outer) with its opening at the bottom, a tapered triangular needle in the ink colour running from just behind a round hub to the inner edge of the band, and the value set large and bold in the opening with a caption under it. Add controls for: Style — Banded (three zones split at two thresholds, filled with an ordinal single-hue ramp from light to dark, no gaps), Progress (pale track of the same hue, accent fill from the start to the value) and Segmented (12 segments with small gaps that light up along the ramp up to the value); Sweep — 180°, 240° or 270° (for 180° put the value under the hub and shrink the SVG height to fit); Needle — Tapered, Line or None; and a Target toggle that draws an ink notch across the band with a small label outside the arc. A labelled range slider sets the value and animates the needle and fill over 400ms with ease-out (instant under prefers-reduced-motion). Print min and max at the arc ends. Give the gauge role=meter with aria values. Hover shows the value, the gap to target and the zone name. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Donut chart (optional labels)

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** donut, part to whole, direct labels, no legend, leader lines, minimal

A clean donut with no legend and the total in the centre. Labels are off by default for a minimal ring with a hover readout; switch them on to name every slice directly with its share, joined by a short leader line.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing how a total splits into 2–6 parts at a glance
- Space for a legend is tight, or a legend would make readers look back and forth
- A minimal ring next to text that already names the parts (labels off)
- One or two slices dominate and that's the message

## Avoid it when
- More than 6 slices (fold the tail into 'Other' or use a ranked bar)
- Slices are similar in size and need precise comparison (use bars)
- Composition across several groups (use 100% stacked bars)

## Anatomy
- Ring about 24% of the radius thick, 2px surface gaps between slices, starting at 12 o'clock, largest first, 'Other' last
- Direct labels outside the ring: name in ink and share in secondary ink, right-aligned on the left side and left-aligned on the right
- Leader lines: 1px from the slice's midpoint to an elbow, then horizontal to the label; labels are spaced so they never overlap
- Centre: the total and its unit; on hover it shows the slice's value instead
- Categorical slots in fixed order; no legend
- Labels off (default): the ring is centred and larger, and slices are named by the hover readout and the centre text

## Data shape
```
[{ name: "Mobile", value: 61200 }, …] — sorted largest first, 'Other' last
```

## Interactions
- Labels switch (Off / On), off by default: on adds the direct labels and leader lines and shrinks the ring to make room
- Dataset switch (Device / Region / Plan) redraws the slices and labels
- Hover a slice or its label: that slice stays full strength, the rest dim, and the centre shows its value and share

## Accessibility
- With labels on, each slice is named and its share printed beside it, so colour never carries identity alone; with labels off, pair the ring with text or a table that names the parts
- SVG aria-label lists every slice with its share
- Hover readout is mirrored by the labels when they are on

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s6`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--axis` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a donut chart with no legend in one self-contained HTML file using inline SVG and no libraries. Seeded data for three datasets (sessions by device, by region, by plan), each 3–6 slices sorted largest first with 'Other' last, coloured by categorical slots in fixed order. A Labels switch (off by default) toggles direct labels; with labels off the ring is centred and larger. Draw the ring about 24% of the radius thick with 2px surface-coloured gaps, starting at 12 o'clock. With labels on, label every slice directly outside the ring: a 1px leader line from the slice's midpoint to an elbow just outside the ring, then horizontal to the label; the label shows the name in ink and the share in secondary ink, right-aligned on the left half and left-aligned on the right half. Space labels on each side so they never overlap (push them apart vertically and keep the leader lines attached). Put the total and its unit in the centre; hovering a slice or its label dims the others and swaps the centre to that slice's value and share. Segmented controls switch labels and datasets. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# KPI donut cards

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** progress to goal, donut, ring, target, kpi card

The standard KPI card with a progress donut: a ring fills toward the goal with the percent in its centre, beside the value, the goal and a delta vs the previous period. Switch between ring-beside and ring-on-top layouts.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Each KPI has a goal and 'how far along are we?' is the headline
- A row of 2–5 goals for the same period (month, quarter, year)
- You want progress cards that sit beside ordinary KPI cards without looking like a different system

## Avoid it when
- Metrics with no goal (use the sparkline KPI card)
- Comparing progress precisely across many goals (use bullet charts or progress bars)
- Values that routinely run far past 100% (the ring caps at full)

## Anatomy
- Same card as the KPI row: 1px hairline border, card radius, label in secondary ink, 28px semibold value
- Donut: a full ring with a pale track in the series hue, the fill starting at 12 o'clock with a round cap; percent of goal in the centre
- A small tick on the ring marks where you should be today (share of the period elapsed)
- Under the value: 'of <goal> goal' and a delta (▲/▼ vs the same point last period, coloured by good/bad)
- Goal met: ring fills fully and a ✓ Goal met note replaces the pace line
- Layout switch: ring beside the text, or ring on top with the text centred

## Data shape
```
[{ label: "Revenue", fmt: money, goal: 2400000, actual: 1840000, prev: 1710000 }, …] per period, plus the share of the period elapsed
```

## Interactions
- Period switch (Month / Quarter / Year) redraws every card
- Layout switch (Beside / On top)
- Hover a ring: actual, goal, remaining, and where pace says you should be today

## Accessibility
- role=meter on each ring with aria-valuenow, -min and -max
- Percent of goal is printed in the ring, never only implied by the arc
- Ahead / behind pace is stated in words, not colour alone

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--track`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--muted`, `--grid`, `--up`, `--down`, `--radius` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a responsive row of KPI donut cards in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Each card follows the standard KPI card (1px hairline border, rounded corners, a secondary-ink label, a 28px semibold value) and adds a progress donut: a full ring with a pale track in the accent hue, the fill starting at 12 o'clock with a round cap, sized by actual ÷ goal and capped at 100%, with the percent of goal printed in the centre. Put a small ink tick on the ring at the share of the period elapsed so readers can see if they're on pace. Under the value print 'of <goal> goal' and a delta vs the same point last period (▲/▼, green when good, red when bad), then a line saying how far ahead or behind pace the metric is; when the goal is met, fill the ring and show '✓ Goal met'. Seeded data for Month, Quarter and Year with a segmented control to switch, and a second control to switch the layout between ring beside the text and ring on top with the text centred. Hover a ring for actual, goal, remaining and expected-by-today. role=meter with aria values. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Gantt chart with progress

**Category:** Charts · **Tags:** gantt, project plan, timeline, schedule, milestones

A project plan as a Gantt chart: a task table (owner, status, due) beside a month timeline where each task's bar fills with its progress, grouped into collapsible phases with tinted bands, milestones as diamonds and a today line.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Showing a project's schedule and how far each task has got
- Status reviews where 'what's late and who owns it?' matters
- 10–40 tasks grouped into a handful of phases

## Avoid it when
- Hundreds of tasks (use a filtered table or a roll-up by phase)
- Dependencies are the main story (use a network or critical-path view)
- Comparing durations precisely (use a sorted bar chart)

## Anatomy
- Left: a task table with Task, Owner, Status and Due columns; phase rows are bold with a ▾ chevron, a people count and the phase's last due date
- Right: a month axis with light gridlines, a today line labelled with the date, and one 28px row per task aligned with the table
- Bars: 12px tall, 3px radius, start to end date; the done share is solid, the rest a pale tint of the same hue
- Phase rows: the whole row tinted with the phase's hue across both panes, with a thin summary bar spanning the phase
- Milestones: a diamond on the due date (zero-length tasks)
- Status: icon + word — ✓ Completed, ◐ In progress, ▲ Delayed (past its end date and not done), ○ Not started
- Colour switch: by phase (categorical slots in order) or by status (status colours, the done share still solid)

## Data shape
```
[{ phase: "Build", task: "Model", owner: "Sofia", start: "2026-10-05", end: "2026-10-23", progress: 0.8 }, …] — status derived from progress, dates and today
```

## Interactions
- Click or press Enter on a phase row to collapse or expand it; Expand all / Collapse all
- Colour switch: Phase / Status
- Hover a bar or a row: dates, duration, progress and status

## Accessibility
- Status is an icon plus a word, never colour alone
- Phase rows are buttons with aria-expanded
- SVG aria-label summarises how many tasks are completed, in progress, delayed and not started

## Design tokens used
`--s1 … --s4`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--muted`, `--grid`, `--good`, `--warn`, `--crit` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a Gantt chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Data: about 16 tasks in 4 phases (Plan, Build, Test, Launch), each with an owner, start and end dates and a progress share; zero-length tasks are milestones. Lay it out as a task table on the left (Task, Owner, Status, Due) aligned row-for-row with a month timeline on the right; 28px rows. Phase rows are bold with a chevron, the number of people and the phase's last due date, and the whole row is tinted with the phase's hue across both panes, with a thin summary bar spanning the phase. Each task bar runs from start to end (12px tall, 3px radius): the done share is solid and the rest a pale tint of the same hue. Milestones are diamonds. # KPI icon cards

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** icon, kpi card, kpi row, delta, scorecard

A full-width row of compact KPI cards, each led by an icon from one consistent line-icon set: the label beside the icon, a large value, a coloured delta (percent or points) and the comparison period. Switch the icon style between tinted badges, coloured outlines and a single neutral ink.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- A scorecard strip across the top of an operational dashboard (6–8 metrics)
- Readers scan for one metric by shape as much as by name
- Metrics mix money, counts, rates and averages and need one shared card

## Avoid it when
- Metrics need a trend to make sense (use the sparkline KPI card)
- Each KPI has a goal (use KPI donut cards)
- Icons would be decoration only, with no consistent meaning across dashboards

## Anatomy
- Card: 1px hairline border, card radius, compact padding; 8 cards wrap to fit the row
- Icon: 24px grid, 2px rounded strokes, no fills, so every icon has the same weight; shown in a 32px tinted circle
- Label beside the icon in secondary ink, wrapping to two lines
- Value: 26px bold display type with tabular figures
- Delta: ▲/▼ with percent change, or pp for rates; green when good and red when bad, where lower is better for metrics like callback rate
- Comparison line: 'vs <previous period dates>' in muted ink

## Data shape
```
[{ label: "Total revenue", icon: "money", fmt: money, cur: 9.34e6, prev: 9.0e6, better: "up" }, …] per period, with the comparison period's date range
```

## Interactions
- Period switch (Month / Quarter / Year to date) redraws every card
- Icon style switch (Badge / Outline / Mono)
- Hover or focus a card: this period, previous period, the change and whether it is good

## Accessibility
- Icons are aria-hidden; every card has an aria-label with the label, value, change and comparison
- Good and bad are stated with ▲/▼ and the tooltip, not colour alone
- Cards are focusable so keyboard users get the same tooltip

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--s3`, `--s4`, `--surface`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--muted`, `--grid`, `--up`, `--down`, `--radius` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a responsive row of eight KPI icon cards in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Each card has a 1px hairline border and rounded corners; at the top an icon in a 32px circle tinted with the icon's colour, with the metric label beside it in secondary ink (wrapping to two lines); then a 26px bold value with tabular figures; then a delta (▲/▼ and percent change, or percentage points for rates) coloured green when good and red when bad, where some metrics are better when lower (callback rate); then 'vs <previous period dates>' in muted ink. Draw all icons from one consistent set on a 24px grid with 2px round-capped strokes and no fills: dollar coin, pie slice, trend arrow, wrench, price tag, person-plus, incoming phone, gauge. Colour icons in a fixed rotation of the first four series colours. Metrics: total revenue, gross margin, net profit, service calls completed, average ticket size, membership revenue, callback rate and technician utilization, with seeded data for Month, Quarter and Year to date and a segmented control to switch. A second control switches the icon style between tinted badges, coloured outlines and one neutral ink colour. Hover or focus a card for this period, the previous period and the change. Icons aria-hidden, an aria-label on every card. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Ask-your-data chat assistant

**Category:** UI patterns · **Tags:** chat, assistant, natural language, AI, Q&A, conversational analytics

An in-dashboard chat panel that answers plain-English questions about the dashboard's data: a value for a period, the monthly trend, the year-over-year change or a split by region, each with an inline chart and a note on how it was calculated. It remembers context, so 'show it trended' and 'what's the YoY change?' follow on from the last answer.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Readers ask ad-hoc questions the fixed charts don't answer
- Executives want one number fast ('what was revenue in Q3?') without filtering
- You plan to put an AI model behind the dashboard and need the front end

## Avoid it when
- The questions are always the same (build the chart instead)
- Numbers must come from an unvetted model (always compute them from the data, as this component does)
- There's no room for a panel at least 320px wide

## Anatomy
- Header: title, data freshness and a Clear button
- Message log (role=log): user questions as right-aligned bubbles, answers with a small assistant mark
- Answer = one-sentence reply with the key numbers in bold, then a card: a KPI (value + delta vs a year earlier), a monthly line chart (dashed line = a year earlier, asked period highlighted), grouped year-over-year columns or ranked region bars
- 'How this was calculated' disclosure under each answer: metric definition, period, comparison period, region, source
- Context line showing what 'it' currently means (metric · period · region)
- Suggestion chips that change with the conversation
- Input with send button; Enter sends, ↑ recalls the last question

## Data shape
```
Monthly rows per region of additive measures { sessions, orders, revenue, newc } (Jan 2024 – Oct 2026). Ratio metrics (AOV, conversion) are computed from summed parts, so any period or region aggregates correctly. Metrics: { key: { label, re (synonyms), calc(sums), f, fs, def } }.
```

## Interactions
- Type a question or click a suggestion; follow-ups reuse the last metric, period and region
- Understands metrics and synonyms (sales, traffic, AOV…), periods (Q3, Q3 2025, last quarter, this month, March, 2025, YTD, last 12 months, last 6 months), regions ('in the West', 'by region') and intents (value, trend, YoY, breakdown, 'which region grew fastest')
- Hover chart points or columns for exact values
- Plug in a model: set window.DC_CHAT = { plan: async (question, context) => ({ intent, metric, period: { from: 'YYYY-MM', to: 'YYYY-MM' }, region }) }; the component still computes and writes every number

## Accessibility
- Message list is role=log with aria-live=polite, so answers are announced
- Input has a label; suggestions are real buttons
- Every chart answer also states its key numbers in the text
- Deltas use ▲/▼ and words (up/down), not colour alone

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--de-emph`, `--surface-2`, `--grid`, `--up`, `--down`, `--border` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an in-dashboard 'ask your data' chat panel in one self-contained HTML file (no libraries, inline SVG). Data: seeded synthetic monthly rows per region (4 regions, Jan 2024 – Oct 2026) of additive measures sessions, orders, revenue and new customers; ratio metrics (AOV = revenue ÷ orders, conversion = orders ÷ sessions) are computed from summed parts. Write a small rule-based question parser: metric synonyms, periods (Q1–Q4 with optional year, last/this quarter, this/last month, month names, a year, YTD, last N months), regions ('in the West'), and intents: value, trend ('show it trended'), year-over-year change, breakdown by region ('which region grew fastest'). Keep conversation context so follow-ups without a metric or period reuse the last ones, and show that context above the input. Each answer is one sentence with bold numbers plus a card: KPI with ▲/▼ delta vs a year earlier; a 12-month line chart with a dashed year-earlier line and the asked period highlighted; grouped year-over-year columns per month; or ranked horizontal region bars with deltas. Under each answer, a 'How this was calculated' disclosure (definition, period, comparison, region, source). Suggestion chips update after each answer. role=log with aria-live, Enter to send, ↑ to recall, Clear button, hover tooltips on charts. Expose window.DC_CHAT.plan(question, context) as an optional hook so an LLM can return the query plan while the component computes every number. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes. Pre-play a sample conversation: 'What was revenue in Q3?', 'Show it to me trended', 'What's the YoY change?'.


---

# US state choropleth map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** map, choropleth, US states, Albers, filter

A filled (choropleth) map of all 50 states and DC on an Albers projection with Alaska and Hawaii inset. Each state is shaded by its value on a sequential scale from zero (or a diverging scale for change), with a gradient legend, an optional value-label layer and click-to-filter.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The question is geographic: which states are high or low, and where they cluster
- Values are rates or shares (normalised), not raw totals
- A dashboard needs a state filter that's also a chart

## Avoid it when
- Values are raw counts that just track population or size (map a rate instead, or use a tile map / bar chart)
- Small states carry the story (they nearly disappear; use a tile map or ranked bars beside the map)
- Readers need exact comparisons (pair it with a ranked list)

## Anatomy
- Real state boundaries as inline SVG paths, separated by thin card-coloured borders
- Sequential fill from the theme's ramp, anchored at 0; 'YoY change' switches to a diverging scale centred on 0
- Gradient legend with the scale ends, plus a No data swatch for grey context shapes
- Show labels Off/On switch: value labels with a contrast-checked ink and halo; tiny shapes skip theirs
- Subtitle turns into 'Filtered to X · Clear' while a filter is set
- Boundary source credit in the footer

## Data shape
```
{ <state id>: { share: 0.142, yoy: 0.011 } }  — keyed by the shape ids (USPS state codes). GEO = { w, h, k: [id, name, d, lx, ly, a, data], s: [[…one array per shape]] }: pre-projected, simplified SVG paths with a label point and area, written by _geo/make_geo.py.
```

## Interactions
- Hover a state: outline plus tooltip with value and rank
- Click (or Enter/Space when focused) to filter to it; others fade to 30%. Click again, Clear or Esc to remove
- The filter is announced as a dc-filter event on window and postMessage({ dcFilter: { id, name } }) to a parent dashboard
- Measure switch (Share / YoY change) and Show labels switch

## Accessibility
- Each state with data is a focusable button with its name and value as the label, and aria-pressed for the filter
- A visually hidden ranked list repeats every value for screen readers
- Labels pick black or white ink against the fill
- Legend states the scale ends in text

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0…--seq-6`, `--div-neg`, `--div-mid`, `--div-pos`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a state choropleth map in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG (no libraries, no network): all 50 states and DC on an Albers projection with Alaska and Hawaii inset. Embed pre-projected, simplified boundary paths with a label point per shape. Shade each state on a sequential colour ramp anchored at 0 (a 'YoY change' measure uses a diverging ramp centred on 0); shapes without data are neutral grey. Thin card-coloured borders between shapes. A gradient legend with the scale ends and a No data swatch. A 'Show labels' Off/On switch adds value labels (black or white ink by contrast, with a halo; skip tiny shapes). Hover shows a tooltip with value and rank; click or Enter/Space filters to that state (others fade to 30%, subtitle reads 'Filtered to X · Clear', Esc clears) and fires a dc-filter CustomEvent plus a parent postMessage. Every state is a focusable button with an aria-label; include a visually hidden ranked list. Credit the boundary source in the footer. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes. Seeded synthetic data.

# US county choropleth map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** map, choropleth, US counties, FIPS, Albers, filter, search

A filled (choropleth) map of all 3,142 US counties (and county equivalents) on an Albers projection with Alaska and Hawaii inset, with state borders drawn on top. Each county is shaded by its value on a sequential scale from zero (or a diverging scale for change), with a gradient legend, an optional value-label layer and click-to-filter.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The question is geographic: which counties are high or low, and where they cluster
- Values are rates or shares (normalised), not raw totals
- A dashboard needs a county filter that's also a chart

## Avoid it when
- Values are raw counts that just track population or size (map a rate instead, or use a tile map / bar chart)
- Small counties carry the story (they nearly disappear; use a tile map or ranked bars beside the map)
- Readers need exact comparisons (pair it with a ranked list)

## Anatomy
- Real county boundaries as inline SVG paths, separated by thin card-coloured borders
- Sequential fill from the theme's ramp, anchored at 0; 'YoY change' switches to a diverging scale centred on 0
- Gradient legend with the scale ends, plus a No data swatch for grey context shapes
- Show labels Off/On switch: value labels with a contrast-checked ink and halo; tiny shapes skip theirs
- Subtitle turns into 'Filtered to X · Clear' while a filter is set
- Boundary source credit in the footer

## Data shape
```
{ <county id>: { share: 0.142, yoy: 0.011 } }  — keyed by the shape ids (5-digit county FIPS codes). GEO = { w, h, k: [id, name, d, lx, ly, a, data], s: [[…one array per shape]], outline }: pre-projected, simplified SVG paths with a label point and area, written by _geo/make_geo.py.
```

## Interactions
- Hover a county: outline plus tooltip with value and rank
- Click (or Enter/Space when focused) to filter to it; others fade to 30%. Click again, Clear or Esc to remove
- Find a county: a search box with every name as a suggestion selects it (replaces one tab stop per shape on this many-shape map)
- The filter is announced as a dc-filter event on window and postMessage({ dcFilter: { id, name } }) to a parent dashboard
- Measure switch (Share / YoY change) and Show labels switch

## Accessibility
- The Find a county search box is the keyboard route to any county; paths are not tab stops
- A visually hidden ranked list repeats every value for screen readers
- Labels pick black or white ink against the fill
- Legend states the scale ends in text

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0…--seq-6`, `--div-neg`, `--div-mid`, `--div-pos`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a county choropleth map in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG (no libraries, no network): all 3,142 US counties (and county equivalents) on an Albers projection with Alaska and Hawaii inset, with state borders drawn on top. Embed pre-projected, simplified boundary paths with a label point per shape. Shade each county on a sequential colour ramp anchored at 0 (a 'YoY change' measure uses a diverging ramp centred on 0); shapes without data are neutral grey. A 'Show labels' Off/On switch adds value labels (black or white ink by contrast, with a halo; skip tiny shapes). Every county is a focusable button with an aria-label; include a visually hidden ranked list. Credit the boundary source in the footer. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes. Seeded synthetic data.

# South America country choropleth map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** map, choropleth, South America, Latin America, countries, filter

A filled (choropleth) map of the 12 South American countries on a Lambert equal-area projection, with French Guiana, the Falkland Islands and Central America as grey context. Each country is shaded by its value on a sequential scale from zero (or a diverging scale for change), with a gradient legend, an optional value-label layer and click-to-filter.

- Real country boundaries as inline SVG paths, separated by thin card-coloured borders
- Sequential fill from the theme's ramp, anchored at 0; 'YoY change' switches to a diverging scale centred on 0
- Gradient legend with the scale ends, plus a No data swatch for grey context shapes
- Show labels Off/On switch: value labels with a contrast-checked ink and halo; tiny shapes skip theirs
- Subtitle turns into 'Filtered to X · Clear' while a filter is set
- Boundary source credit in the footer

## Data shape
```
{ <country id>: { share: 0.142, yoy: 0.011 } }  — keyed by the shape ids (country names). GEO = { w, h, k: [id, name, d, lx, ly, a, data], s: [[…one array per shape]] }: pre-projected, simplified SVG paths with a label point and area, written by _geo/make_geo.py.
```

## Interactions
- Hover a country: outline plus tooltip with value and rank
- Click (or Enter/Space when focused) to filter to it; others fade to 30%. Click again, Clear or Esc to remove
- The filter is announced as a dc-filter event on window and postMessage({ dcFilter: { id, name } }) to a parent dashboard
- Measure switch (Share / YoY change) and Show labels switch

## Accessibility
- Each country with data is a focusable button with its name and value as the label, and aria-pressed for the filter
- A visually hidden ranked list repeats every value for screen readers
- Labels pick black or white ink against the fill
- Legend states the scale ends in text

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0…--seq-6`, `--div-neg`, `--div-mid`, `--div-pos`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

Embed pre-projected, simplified boundary paths with a label point per shape. Seeded synthetic data.

# Africa country choropleth map

**Category:** Maps · **Tags:** map, choropleth, Africa, countries, filter

A filled (choropleth) map of all 54 African countries on a Lambert equal-area projection (island states as dots where too small to draw), with Western Sahara, Somaliland, southern Europe and the Middle East as grey context. Each country is shaded by its value on a sequential scale from zero (or a diverging scale for change), with a gradient legend, an optional value-label layer and click-to-filter.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- The question is geographic: which countries are high or low, and where they cluster
- Values are rates or shares (normalised), not raw totals
- A dashboard needs a country filter that's also a chart

## Avoid it when
- Values are raw counts that just track population or size (map a rate instead, or use a tile map / bar chart)
- Small countries carry the story (they nearly disappear; use a tile map or ranked bars beside the map)
- Readers need exact comparisons (pair it with a ranked list)

## Anatomy
- Real country boundaries as inline SVG paths, separated by thin card-coloured borders
- Sequential fill from the theme's ramp, anchored at 0; 'YoY change' switches to a diverging scale centred on 0
- Gradient legend with the scale ends, plus a No data swatch for grey context shapes
- Show labels Off/On switch: value labels with a contrast-checked ink and halo; tiny shapes skip theirs
- Subtitle turns into 'Filtered to X · Clear' while a filter is set
- Boundary source credit in the footer

## Data shape
```
{ <country id>: { share: 0.142, yoy: 0.011 } }  — keyed by the shape ids (country names). GEO = { w, h, k: [id, name, d, lx, ly, a, data], s: [[…one array per shape]] }: pre-projected, simplified SVG paths with a label point and area, written by _geo/make_geo.py.
```

## Interactions
- Hover a country: outline plus tooltip with value and rank
- Click (or Enter/Space when focused) to filter to it; others fade to 30%. Click again, Clear or Esc to remove
- Find a country: a search box with every name as a suggestion selects it (replaces one tab stop per shape on this many-shape map)
- The filter is announced as a dc-filter event on window and postMessage({ dcFilter: { id, name } }) to a parent dashboard
- Measure switch (Share / YoY change) and Show labels switch

## Accessibility
- The Find a country search box is the keyboard route to any country; paths are not tab stops
- A visually hidden ranked list repeats every value for screen readers
- Labels pick black or white ink against the fill
- Legend states the scale ends in text

## Design tokens used
`--seq-0…--seq-6`, `--div-neg`, `--div-mid`, `--div-pos`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--ink` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt

# Aging buckets KPI card

**Category:** KPI cards · **Tags:** accounts receivable, aging, DSO, stacked bar, status colours, finance, toggle

An accounts-receivable aging card: open total and DSO up top, one tall 100% bar split into Current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days in a green-to-red status ramp, bucket totals beneath, and an optional list of the largest open balances, each with its own aging mix and its oldest bucket.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Money or work is sorted into ordered age bands that get worse with time (receivables, payables, open tickets, backlog, inventory age)
- The headline is how much is current vs overdue, with the biggest contributors one glance below
- Finance or ops dashboards where DSO (or another age metric) sits beside the total

## Avoid it when
- The categories aren't ordered by severity (use the breakdown bar with categorical colours)
- More than 6 bands
- You need the trend of aging over time (use a stacked area or column chart by month)

## Anatomy
- Header: title, open total and invoice count; the age metric (DSO) right-aligned at 28px bold with its change vs last month coloured by whether it's good
- A 44px 100% bar: one rounded segment per bucket with 3px gaps, the share printed inside segments of 12% or more
- Bucket legend: swatch, monospaced band label, total at 20px bold
- Optional detail (Top balances: Show / Hide): customer, open amount, a 12px 100% bar of that customer's aging mix, and the oldest bucket it has, in that bucket's colour

## Data shape
```
{ total, invoices, dso: 52, dsoPrev: 49, buckets: [{ key: "cur", label: "Current", value: 3810000 }, … ], top: [{ name: "Cedarline Foods", split: [312000, 158000, 61000, 43000, 0] }, …] }  — split is one amount per bucket, in bucket order.
```

## Interactions
- Hover or focus a bucket (bar segment or legend item): that bucket stays full strength in the main bar, the legend and every customer bar; the rest fade to 30%
- Hover any segment for a tooltip with amount and share
- Top balances: Show / Hide switches the bottom section on or off

## Accessibility
- Every bucket total is in the legend as text; the bars are summaries
- The status ramp is never the only cue: band labels are printed and the oldest bucket is named in words
- Legend items are focusable and highlight on focus as well as hover

## Design tokens used
`--good`, `--warn`, `--serious`, `--crit`, `--surface`, `--ink-2`, `--muted`, `--up`, `--down` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build an accounts-receivable aging KPI card in one self-contained HTML file. Header: title 'Receivables aging', a subline with the open total and invoice count, and the DSO right-aligned (28px bold) with its change vs last month (fewer days is good, coloured accordingly). Below, one 44px-tall 100% bar split into five ordered buckets (Current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, 90+) coloured green → lime → amber → orange → red from status tokens, 3px gaps, 8px rounding on every segment, the share printed inside segments of at least 12%. Under it a five-column legend: swatch, monospaced band label, total (20px bold). Then an optional 'Top open balances' list (toggle Show / Hide in the header): customer name, open amount, a 12px 100% bar of that customer's aging mix, and the oldest bucket it carries in that bucket's colour. Hovering or focusing a bucket highlights it everywhere and fades the rest to 30%; tooltips give amount and share. CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.

# Lollipop chart

**Category:** Basic charts · **Tags:** lollipop, dot plot, ranking, deviation, bar alternative

A bar chart's lighter cousin: a thin stem and a prominent dot per category, sorted by value. Switch between columns and rows, stem from zero or from the average (a diverging view that colours each side), and click a lollipop to highlight it while everything else steps back.

Live demo: [`index.html`](index.html) — one self-contained file, no dependencies. Light and dark themes; add `?theme=dark` or `?embed=1` to the URL.

## Use it when
- Ranking 6–25 categories where many bars would look heavy
- The end value matters more than the filled area
- Showing how each category sits above or below an average or target

## Avoid it when
- Values that are close together (the dots overlap; use bars or a dot plot with a zoomed axis)
- Part-to-whole comparisons (use stacked bars or a waffle)
- Negative and positive values on a zero baseline with no reference (use diverging bars)

## Anatomy
- Stems: 2px lines in the series colour from the baseline to the value; dots: 12px circles with a 2px surface ring so they read over gridlines
- Baseline: zero (axis line) or the average (a dashed reference line labelled with its value); in average mode stems above use --s1 and below use --s2, named in a legend
- Sorted by value by default, with an A–Z option; long labels switch the chart to rows
- Value labels at the dot end; gridlines in --grid along the value axis only
- Highlight: the clicked lollipop keeps its colour and gains a label, the rest turn --de-emph
- On load the stems grow from the baseline once (skipped for reduced motion)

## Data shape
```
[{ port: "Singapore", days: 3.1 }, …] plus the optional reference value (average or target)
```

## Interactions
- Orientation switch: Columns / Rows
- Baseline switch: Zero / Average
- Sort switch: By value / A–Z
- Click a lollipop (or press Enter on it) to highlight it; click again to clear
- Hover for the value and its difference from the average

## Accessibility
- The svg has an aria-label naming the top and bottom categories
- Each lollipop is a focusable group with its own aria-label
- Above / below average is shown by position and the legend, not colour alone
- Growth animation respects prefers-reduced-motion

## Design tokens used
`--s1`, `--s2`, `--de-emph`, `--grid`, `--axis`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--muted`, `--surface` — defined once on `:root` in the demo, with dark-mode values.

## Prompt
Paste this into Claude, Cursor or any coding assistant (attach `index.html` as a reference for an exact match):

> Build a lollipop chart in one self-contained HTML file with inline SVG and no libraries. Twelve container ports with an average dwell time in days, sorted by value. Each category is a 2px stem in the accent colour from the baseline to the value, ending in a 12px dot with a 2px ring in the card surface colour, with the value labelled past the dot; gridlines only along the value axis. Add three segmented controls: Columns / Rows (rows put long labels on the left), Zero / Average baseline (average mode draws a dashed reference line with its value and stems out from it, accent colour above and a second colour below, with a legend), and By value / A–Z sort. Clicking a lollipop highlights it (others turn a muted grey) and clicking again clears; hovering shows the value and the difference from the average. Stems grow from the baseline once on load, skipped under prefers-reduced-motion. Focusable lollipops with aria-labels, CSS variables for every colour, light and dark themes.
